en.text: Which one of the following Carnatic music ragas is similar to Raga Bilawal in Hindustani music?
en.explanation:
Answer: (d) Dheera Shankarabharanam. Bilawal uses all seven shuddha (natural) notes of Hindustani music, and Dheera Shankarabharanam has the same scale, the Western major scale.

Hindustani music groups ragas under ten parent scales called thaats, a scheme set out by V.N. Bhatkhande; Carnatic music uses 72 melakartas. Bilawal, the thaat of all natural notes, is the reference scale and matches the 29th melakarta, Dheera Shankarabharanam. Other pairs: Kalyan and Kalyani, Khamaj and Harikambhoji, Kafi and Kharaharapriya, Asavari and Nat Bhairavi, Bhairavi and Hanumatodi, Purvi and Kamavardhini.

The trap: (a) is tempting because Nat Bhairavi's name echoes the Hindustani Bhairavi, but its scale matches the Asavari thaat; the Carnatic match for the Bhairavi thaat is Hanumatodi.

Read more: Nitin Singhania, Indian Art and Culture, on Hindustani and Carnatic music.

en.text: The artificially fixed rupee-sterling exchange rate prescribed by the Hilton-Young Commission (1926) was adopted by the British Government for which one of the following reasons?
options: Aiding the flow of remittances from India and maintaining India’s creditworthiness
Encouraging export of cotton produce from India
Preventing depreciation of the Rupee in terms of gold
en.explanation:
Answer: (a) Aiding the flow of remittances from India and maintaining India’s creditworthiness. A dearer rupee meant fewer rupees for every pound India paid to Britain.

The Hilton Young Commission (Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance) fixed the rupee at 1s 6d instead of the pre-war 1s 4d, and the Currency Act of 1927 made it law. The higher rate cut the rupee cost of India's sterling payments to Britain, the Home Charges, but made Indian exports dearer; Purshotamdas Thakurdas, an Indian member, dissented in favour of 1s 4d. The Commission also proposed a central bank, which became the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in 1935.

The trap: (d) is tempting because the Commission also proposed a gold bullion standard, but the high 1s 6d rate itself served to ease India's sterling payments to Britain and keep its credit sound in London.

Read more: Reserve Bank of India, History of the Reserve Bank of India, Volume 1 (1935–51), on its origins in the Hilton Young Commission.

en.text:
Consider the following statements:
I. Pali texts contain the first definite references to coins, e.g., kahapana, nikkha, kamsa, and kakanika.
II. The literary evidence from Pali texts is corroborated by archaeological evidence of punch-marked coins from many sites, most of them made of silver.
The above statements have been associated with which of the following?
1. Emergence of urban life
2. Transition to money economy
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (c) Both 1 and 2. Coins came with the growth of towns in the Ganga valley and the shift from barter to money.

  • Item I: yes. Coins appear with the second urbanisation of the 6th century BCE, when towns in the middle Ganga plains grew as centres of trade, crafts and rule.
  • Item II: yes. Punch-marked coins, mostly of silver, show exchange moving from barter to money, which the trade of the new towns needed.

Around the 6th century BCE the middle Ganga plains saw a second urbanisation, the first since the Harappan cities, with towns such as Rajagriha, Shravasti, Kaushambi and Champa. Punch-marked coins of silver and copper, from about this time, are the earliest Indian coins, and Pali texts name coins such as the kahapana. Towns and money grew together.

The trap: (b) is tempting because coins look like a purely economic sign, but money spread with the trade of the new towns, so the evidence reflects urban life as well as a money economy.

Read more: NCERT Class 12, Themes in Indian History Part I, Chapter 2, Kings, Farmers and Towns.

en.text:
Which of the following temples has/have a Nagara-style shikhara?
1. Malegitti Shivalaya, Badami
2. Huchimalligudi Temple, Aihole
3. Dashavatara Temple, Deogarh
4. Virupaksha Temple, Pattadakal
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (b) 2 and 3. Huchimalligudi and the Deogarh Dashavatara temple have curved northern shikharas; the other two are Dravida temples.

  • Item 1: no. Malegitti Shivalaya at Badami, a 7th-century early Chalukya temple, is in the Dravida style, with a storeyed vimana rather than a curved northern tower.
  • Item 2: yes. Huchimalligudi at Aihole, an early Chalukya Shiva temple, has a curvilinear rekha-nagara shikhara over its sanctum.
  • Item 3: yes. The Dashavatara temple at Deogarh (Uttar Pradesh), from the early 6th century, had a curvilinear latina (rekha-prasada) shikhara, now partly ruined, a classic early Nagara form.
  • Item 4: no. The Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal, built in the 8th century by Queen Lokamahadevi to mark Vikramaditya II's victory over the Pallavas, is in the Dravida style.

Temple styles are told apart by the tower. Nagara (northern) temples have a curvilinear shikhara of the latina or rekha-prasada type; Dravida (southern) temples have a stepped, pyramidal vimana topped by a small dome. The early Chalukyas of Badami built in both styles side by side at Aihole, Badami and Pattadakal, so a temple's site alone does not tell its style.

The trap: (d) is tempting because Pattadakal does have northern-style temples, but its Virupaksha temple is Dravida, said to be modelled on the Kailasanatha temple at Kanchipuram.

Read more: NCERT Class 11, An Introduction to Indian Art Part I, chapter Temple Architecture and Sculpture.

en.text: Among the four main forms of existence of life recognized in Jainism, which one of the following is not included?
en.explanation:
Answer: (b) Yaksha (demi-gods). The four gatis are deva, manushya, naraki (hell-beings) and tiryancha; yakshas are a kind of deva.

Jainism teaches that each soul (jiva) is reborn, according to its karma, in one of four gatis: heavenly beings (deva), humans (manushya), hell-beings (naraki) and tiryancha, which covers animals, plants and even the tiniest life forms. Only a human birth can lead to liberation. Jain ethics stress non-violence towards all beings because every living thing, even plants and water, has a soul.

The trap: (d) is tempting because plants seem out of place in a list of life forms, but Jainism counts animals, plants and micro-organisms together as tiryancha, since it holds that all of them have souls.

Read more: Padmanabh S. Jaini, The Jaina Path of Purification, on karma, rebirth and the four gatis.

en.text: The Hallisalasya painting in the Bagh Caves represents:
options: The depiction of Shiva and Parvati on Kailasha
en.explanation:
Answer: (a) A joyous folk dance. The Hallisalasya mural in Bagh Cave 4 shows a circular group dance with musicians.

The Bagh caves in Dhar district, Madhya Pradesh, are Buddhist rock-cut monasteries whose 5th–6th century murals belong to the same tradition as Ajanta. Besides religious themes they show secular life, such as the Hallisalasya group dance in Cave 4, the Rang Mahal.

The trap: (b) is tempting because the Bagh caves are Buddhist monasteries, but the Hallisalasya panel is a secular scene of dancers and musicians, not an image of the Buddha.

Read more: Nitin Singhania, Indian Art and Culture, on Indian mural painting (Ajanta and Bagh).

en.text:
Consider the following statements relating to the use of the place-value system in India:
1. The earliest epigraphic use of the place-value system in India is found in the Mankani plates from Gujarat (AD 595 – 596).
2. In the ninth century, place-values become general in inscriptions all over India.
3. The place-values have been found in Sanskrit inscriptions in South-east Asia as early as the seventh century.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
en.explanation:
Answer: (d) 1, 2 and 3. Place value appears in a Gujarat grant of AD 595–596, is general in Indian inscriptions by the 9th century, and in South-east Asia by the 7th.

  • Statement 1: correct. The Mankani copper plates of Taralasvamin, dated year 346 of the Kalachuri era (AD 595–596), give the date in words and in place-value figures, the earliest such epigraphic use usually cited.
  • Statement 2: correct. From the 9th century place-value numerals are the norm in Indian inscriptions; the Gwalior Chaturbhuj temple inscription of 876 CE even writes zero as a small circle.
  • Statement 3: correct. A 7th-century Sanskrit inscription of Cambodia writes the Saka years 526 and 546 (604 and 624 CE) in word numerals set out by place value; the Sambor stele of 683 CE, in Old Khmer, uses digits with a dot for zero.

The decimal place-value system with a sign for zero is among India's great gifts to mathematics. In inscriptions it appears from the late 6th century, becomes general by the 9th, and is found in South-east Asia by the 7th. Through the Arabs it reached Europe as the Hindu-Arabic numerals used today.

The trap: (a) is tempting because South-east Asia seems an unlikely place to use the system before it was general in India, but a Cambodian inscription of 683 CE already writes a place-value date with a zero.

A note: The epigraphist V.V. Mirashi judged the Mankani plates a likely 8th-century forgery, so their claim to be the earliest use is contested; the standard account, which the question follows, accepts it.

Read more: A.L. Basham, The Wonder That Was India, on Indian mathematics and numerals.

en.text:
Consider the following statements about the archaeological findings in Harappan towns:
I. There is wide occurrence of spindle-whorls in the houses but absence of spinning wheels.
II. Weights and measurement scales, complete with graduations have been discovered.
III. There are houses built in large part with baked bricks, around relatively spacious courtyards, with their own wells, bathing platforms, and large rooms.
Which of the following inferences can be drawn from the above statements?
1. Statement I suggests that spinning was a laborious activity done at home.
2. Statement II suggests the extent of the scientific knowledge that the Harappans possessed.
3. Statement III suggests the emergence of a common property system.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (a) 1 and 2 only. Spindle whorls point to home spinning and graduated weights to measuring skill; the large houses point to private, not common, property.

  • Statement I: correct. Spindle whorls in many houses show thread was spun by hand at home; with no spinning wheel, spinning was slow, laborious work.
  • Statement II: correct. Standard cubical chert weights and graduated scales show precise measurement, a sign of the Harappans' technical and mathematical knowledge.
  • Statement III: incorrect. Private wells, bathing platforms and spacious courtyards in individual houses point to private family property and differences in wealth, not property held in common.

Inference questions ask what a piece of evidence can actually show. Harappan houses were private, inward-looking homes, many with their own wells (Mohenjodaro had about 700) and bathing areas, while cubical chert weights followed a binary system for small units and a decimal one for large. Such finds speak of crafts, trade, skill and social differences, not of common ownership.

The trap: (d) is tempting because planned Harappan towns suggest collective control, but houses with their own wells and baths point to private, not common, property.

Read more: NCERT Class 12, Themes in Indian History Part I, Chapter 1, Bricks, Beads and Bones.

en.text: Which one of the following statements about the Eka Movement and Bardoli Satyagraha is correct?
options: The Eka Movement was throughout supported and organized by the Congress while Bardoli Satyagraha was initially independent of Congress influence and was only in the last stages supported by the Congress.
The Eka Movement was provided leadership by the taluqdars of Awadh, whereas the Bardoli Satyagraha was a movement of the landless labourers.
The Bardoli Satyagraha was a campaign against the enhancement of land revenue, while the Eka Movement was a protest against excessive extraction of rents.
The Eka Movement was located in the Varanasi and Mirzapur districts of the present-day U.P., while the Bardoli Satyagraha took place in Saurashtra.
en.explanation:
Answer: (c) The Bardoli Satyagraha was a campaign against the enhancement of land revenue, while the Eka Movement was a protest against excessive extraction of rents. Revenue went to the state, rent to landlords.

Peasant protest followed the land system. In Awadh's taluqdari areas tenants paid rent to landlords: the Eka (unity) movement of 1921–22 in Hardoi, Bahraich, Sitapur and Barabanki, led by Madari Pasi, fought rents far above the recorded rates and the oppression of rent collectors. In Gujarat's ryotwari areas peasants paid revenue to the state: the Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928 in Surat district, led by Vallabhbhai Patel, fought a revenue hike of about 22 per cent, later cut to 6.03 per cent.

The trap: (a) is tempting because Congress and Khilafat leaders did start the Eka meetings, but the movement soon passed out of their hands to Madari Pasi and other low-caste leaders.

Read more: Spectrum's A Brief History of Modern India (Rajiv Ahir), on the peasant movements of the 1920s.

en.text:
Consider the following statements about the Rigvedic period:
I. Irrigation from wells allowed agriculture to expand away from flood plains and strips on river margins into the present Punjab and Haryana plains having underground water levels reasonably close to the surface.
II. Draught-animal power was employed to draw up water out of the wells.
Which of the following information support/supports the above statements?
1. There is evidence in the Rigveda of the use of ashma chakra (stone pulley wheel) and ahava (strapped wooden pails) to draw up water.
2. Mention has been made in the Rigveda of the use of implements like parashu/kulisha (axe) and datra /sreni (sickle).
3. There is a history of the use of ox, even before the Rigveda, for ploughing the land and pulling the carts.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (c) 1 and 3 only. The pulley and pails show well irrigation and the ox shows draught power; axes and sickles show neither.

  • Statement I: correct. A stone pulley wheel (ashma chakra) and strapped wooden pails (ahava) are the gear of wells worked with a pulley, which supports the use of wells for irrigation.
  • Statement II: incorrect. Axes (parashu, kulisha) and sickles (datra, sreni) are tools for clearing and harvesting; they say nothing about wells or the power used to lift water.
  • Statement III: correct. Oxen drew ploughs and carts from Harappan times (terracotta plough models, a ploughed field at Kalibangan), so animal power to work a well-pulley was already at hand.

Rigvedic people were mainly pastoral but also farmed. Wells worked with a pulley wheel and pails would let farming spread from river margins into the Punjab and Haryana plains, where ground water lay close to the surface, and oxen, long used for ploughs and carts, could supply the power. In such questions keep only the evidence that bears on the exact claim.

The trap: (b) is tempting because axes and sickles are farm tools, but they show clearing and harvesting, not how water was drawn from wells or by what power.

Read more: Irfan Habib and Vijay Kumar Thakur, The Vedic Age (A People's History of India, Volume 3).

I. कूपों से की जाने वाली सिंचाई ने कृषि को प्लावनीय मैदानों और नदी किनारों की पट्टियों से दूर वर्तमान पंजाब और हरियाणा के मैदानों में विस्तृत होने का अवसर दिया जहाँ भूमिगत जल स्तर सतह के पर्याप्त समीप था।
II. कूपों से पानी निकालने के लिए भारवाही-पशु शक्ति का प्रयोग किया गया।
निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी सूचना, उपर्युक्त कथनों का समर्थन करती है/हैं?

en.text:
Consider the following assertion:
In the Pleistocene period either the Yamuna once flowed into the Indus, or the Sutlej flowed into the Yamuna and one major tributary of either had shifted from the Ganga to the Indus or vice versa.
Which of the following is/are the basis of the above assertion?
1. The Nadi-Sukta of the Rigveda
2. The explorations of the Sutlej and the Yamuna by Robert Bruce Foote
3. The presence of the same species of dolphins in both the Indus and the Ganga river systems
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (d) 3. River dolphins of one lineage in both the Indus and Ganga systems show that the two basins were once linked.

  • Item 1: no. The Nadi Sukta (Rigveda, Book 10) only lists rivers from the Ganga to the Indus; composed long after the Pleistocene, it records no change in their courses.
  • Item 2: no. Robert Bruce Foote, the father of Indian prehistory, found India's first Palaeolithic hand-axe at Pallavaram near Madras in 1863; his work lay in southern and western India, not on these rivers.
  • Item 3: yes. River dolphins of one genus, Platanista, live in both the Indus and the Ganga systems; freshwater animals could reach both only if the basins were once joined by a river.

Rivers near the low divide between the Indus and Ganga systems have changed course: the Yamuna and the Sutlej are thought to have once flowed into the other system or into the now-dry Ghaggar-Hakra. A freshwater animal shared by both basins is strong evidence of such a link. The Indus and Ganges river dolphins were long treated as one species; a 2021 study split them into two, finding they had been apart for about half a million years, within the Pleistocene.

The trap: (a) is tempting because the Nadi Sukta names the Yamuna and the Sutlej (Shutudri), but this Vedic hymn only lists rivers; it says nothing about their courses in the Pleistocene.

Read more: NCERT Class 11, India: Physical Environment, chapter Drainage System, on the Indo-Brahma river and the Indus–Ganga divide.

en.text: What does an empty seat represent in early Buddhist iconography?
en.explanation:
Answer: (a) The meditation of the Buddha. Early art showed the Buddha through symbols, and the empty seat stood for him in meditation.

Early Buddhist sculpture at Bharhut and Sanchi (2nd–1st century BCE) did not show the Buddha in human form but through symbols: the empty seat for his meditation, the stupa for the mahaparinibbana, the wheel for the first sermon at Sarnath and the tree for his enlightenment. Images of the Buddha in human form came later, around the 1st century CE, at Mathura and in Gandhara.

The trap: (c) is tempting because an empty seat seems to mark the Buddha's absence, but early art used the stupa for the Mahaparinibbana; the wheel stood for the First Sermon and a riderless horse for the Mahabhinishkramana.

Which of the following pairs of ancient and modern names of rivers is/are correctly matched?
1. Vitasta : Chenab
2. Asikni : Jhelum
3. Parushni : Ravi
4. Yavyavati : Beas
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (c) 3 only. Parushni is the Rigvedic name of the Ravi; the other three pairs are mismatched.

  • Pair 1: not correctly matched. Vitasta is the Jhelum; the Chenab was called Asikni, and later Chandrabhaga.
  • Pair 2: not correctly matched. Asikni is the Chenab; the Jhelum was called Vitasta.
  • Pair 3: correctly matched. Parushni, the Rigvedic Ravi (later called Iravati), is the river beside which the Battle of Ten Kings was fought.
  • Pair 4: not correctly matched. The Beas was called Vipash, later Vipasha; Yavyavati is not the Beas.

The Rigveda names the Punjab rivers by older names. From west to east they are Vitasta (Jhelum), Asikni (Chenab), Parushni (Ravi), Vipash (Beas) and Shutudri (Sutlej), with Sindhu for the Indus and the Sarasvati further east. Later texts gave some of them new names, such as Chandrabhaga for the Chenab and Iravati for the Ravi.

The trap: (a) is tempting because Vitasta and Asikni are genuine Rigvedic river names, but they are swapped: Vitasta is the Jhelum and Asikni the Chenab.

Read more: R.S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past, on the geography of the Rig Vedic age.

en.text:
Which of the following statements on the Amaravati Stupa and its relief sculpture is/are correct?
1. It was located in the lower Krishna valley.
2. In India, it was next only to the Sanchi Stupa in size.
3. The Amaravati school of sculpture made a lasting impact on the later South Indian sculpture, and its products were carried to Sri Lanka and South-east Asia.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (b) 1 and 3 only. Amaravati lay in the lower Krishna valley and its art spread far, but it was larger than Sanchi, not second to it.

  • Statement 1: correct. Amaravati stands on the south bank of the Krishna in Andhra Pradesh, in the river's lower valley.
  • Statement 2: incorrect. The Amaravati stupa's circular base was about 49 m (162 ft) across, against about 37 m (120 ft) for the Great Stupa at Sanchi, so it was larger, not second.
  • Statement 3: correct. The Amaravati (Andhra) style of limestone relief shaped later South Indian sculpture, and its works and style travelled to Sri Lanka and South-east Asia.

Early Indian sculpture had three great schools: Gandhara (grey schist, Greco-Roman influence), Mathura (red sandstone) and Amaravati (white limestone) in the Krishna valley, which flourished under Satavahana-era patronage. Amaravati is known for lively narrative reliefs of the Buddha's life. Many of its panels, including the 'Elliot marbles' collected by Walter Elliot in 1845, are now in the Government Museum, Chennai, and the British Museum.

The trap: (d) is tempting because Amaravati was among the grandest stupas of India, but statement 2 understates it: it was bigger than the Great Stupa at Sanchi, not second to it.

Read more: NCERT Class 11, An Introduction to Indian Art Part I, chapter Post-Mauryan Trends in Indian Art and Architecture.

Which of the following pairs of the king and his dynasty in early historical Tamilakam is/are not correctly matched?
1. Senguttuvan : Chera
2. Udiyanjeral : Chola
3. Nedunjeliyan : Pandya
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (b) 2 only. Udiyanjeral was a Chera king, not a Chola; the other two pairs are right.

  • Pair 1: correctly matched. Senguttuvan, the 'Red Chera' of the Silappadikaram, is the Chera king credited with starting the worship of Kannagi as the goddess Pattini.
  • Pair 2: not correctly matched. Udiyanjeral was one of the earliest Chera kings, praised in Sangam poetry for feeding the armies at Kurukshetra; he was not a Chola.
  • Pair 3: correctly matched. Nedunjeliyan was a Pandya king of Madurai; a ruler of that name won the Battle of Talaiyalanganam against the Cheras and Cholas.

Sangam texts describe three crowned kingdoms of Tamilakam: the Cholas of the Kaveri delta (capital Uraiyur, port Puhar, emblem the tiger, best-known king Karikala), the Cheras of Kerala (capital Vanji, port Muziris, emblem the bow) and the Pandyas of the far south (capital Madurai, port Korkai, emblem the fish). Senguttuvan and Udiyanjeral were Cheras; Nedunjeliyan was a Pandya.

The trap: (a) is tempting because the Silappadikaram story begins in Puhar, the Chola port, but Senguttuvan, who honoured Kannagi, was a Chera king.

Read more: R.S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past, on the Sangam age and the Chera, Chola and Pandya kingdoms.

en.text:
Which of the following factors contributed to the formation of the Forward Bloc by Subhas Chandra Bose in 1939?
1. Bose failed to win the confidence of Mahatma Gandhi.
2. The Congress Left was disunited and failed to support Bose.
3. The Communists did not support Bose in his endeavours.
4. The supporters of M.N. Roy and socialist leaders like Jayaprakash Narayan preferred Congress unity to supporting Bose.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (b) 1, 2 and 4. Without Gandhi's backing and with the Left divided, Bose resigned in April 1939 and formed the Forward Bloc in May.

  • Statement 1: correct. Bose beat Gandhi's candidate Pattabhi Sitaramayya in January 1939; Gandhi called it his own defeat, and the Pant resolution asked Bose to choose his Working Committee as Gandhi wished.
  • Statement 2: correct. The Left did not stand together behind Bose at the Tripuri session of March 1939, so the Pant resolution passed and he was left isolated.
  • Statement 3: incorrect. The Communists had backed Bose in his January 1939 re-election; the refusal that hurt him at Tripuri came from the Congress Socialists and M.N. Roy's followers.
  • Statement 4: correct. At Tripuri, Jayaprakash Narayan's Congress Socialists stayed neutral on the Pant resolution to keep the Congress united, and M.N. Roy's followers also put unity before Bose.

Bose's re-election in 1939 against Gandhi's nominee opened the Tripuri crisis. Most of the Congress Working Committee resigned, the Pant resolution asked Bose to name a new one in line with Gandhi's wishes, and with the Left split he resigned on 29 April 1939. On 3 May he formed the Forward Bloc as a left group inside the Congress.

The trap: (a) is tempting because the Left as a whole failed Bose, but it was the Congress Socialists and the Royists who put Congress unity first, while the Communists had backed his re-election.

Read more: Spectrum's A Brief History of Modern India (Rajiv Ahir), on the Tripuri crisis of 1939.

en.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the British policy in Awadh immediately after its annexation in 1856:
1. The taluqdars were dispossessed of their estates but allowed to retain their arms and forts.
2. A Summary Revenue Settlement was made in 1856 assuming that the taluqdars were outsiders.
3. The British believed in taking revenue directly from the peasants by removing the taluqdars.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
en.explanation:
Answer: (a) 2 and 3 only. The 1856 Summary Settlement treated the taluqdars as interlopers and tried to settle the land with its actual owners.

  • Statement 1: incorrect. Immediately after annexation the taluqdars were disarmed and their forts destroyed, besides losing land.
  • Statement 2: correct. The Summary Settlement of 1856 assumed the taluqdars were interlopers who had seized land by force and fraud and had no permanent stake in it.
  • Statement 3: correct. The settlement set out to remove the taluqdars wherever possible and settle the land with the actual owners, so revenue would come directly from the cultivators.

The British annexed Awadh in 1856 on the charge of misgovernment and exiled Nawab Wajid Ali Shah to Calcutta. The Summary Settlement cut the taluqdars' share of Awadh's villages from 67 per cent to 38 per cent. Dispossessed taluqdars and their peasants then fought together, making Awadh a stronghold of the 1857 revolt.

The trap: (c) is tempting because the British did strip the taluqdars of their estates, but they also disarmed them and destroyed their forts, so statement 1 fails.

Read more: NCERT Class 12, Themes in Indian History Part III, chapter Rebels and the Raj.

en.text:
Consider the following assertion:
The genesis of political alliances based on community lay in the very nature of the Montague-Chelmsford Reforms, 1919.
Which of the following statements support/supports the above assertion?
1. Reforms retained and extended the principle of separate electorates.
2. Separate electorates were supposed to counter Indian nationalism, which was growing stronger.
3. Deprived classes rallied around the favours inherent in separate electorates.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (d) 1, 2 and 3. The 1919 reforms extended separate electorates, which divided nationalist ranks and drew communities to organise for their share.

  • Statement 1: correct. The Government of India Act 1919 kept separate electorates for Muslims, begun in 1909, and extended them to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans.
  • Statement 2: correct. The British used separate electorates to divide Indians along community lines and so weaken a national movement that was gaining strength.
  • Statement 3: correct. Groups that felt left out organised for a share: the non-Brahmin Justice Party of Madras demanded a separate electorate like the Muslims', won 28 reserved seats in general constituencies instead, and took power in 1920.

Separate electorates let only members of a community vote for its reserved seats. Begun for Muslims by the Morley-Minto Reforms (1909), they were extended in 1919 and offered to the Depressed Classes by the Communal Award of 1932, which the Poona Pact replaced with reserved seats in a joint electorate. Each step pushed Indian politics further along community lines.

The trap: (a) is tempting because statement 1 is the plain constitutional fact, but statements 2 and 3 give the British motive and the communities' response that together bred community-based alliances.

Read more: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity, Chapter 1, Historical Background (the Government of India Act of 1919).

en.text: Pandit Mallikarjun Mansur, the famous classical singer from Karnataka, represented the:
en.explanation:
Answer: (d) Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana. Mansur, from near Dharwad, learnt this style from Manji Khan and Bhurji Khan, sons of its founder Alladiya Khan.

Gharanas are lineages of style in Hindustani vocal music, among them Gwalior (the oldest khayal gharana), Agra, Kirana, Patiala and Jaipur-Atrauli. Jaipur-Atrauli, founded by Alladiya Khan, is known for intricate melodic patterns and rare ragas; Kesarbai Kerkar, Mogubai Kurdikar and Kishori Amonkar also sang in it. The Dharwad region of Karnataka also gave Hindustani music Gangubai Hangal and Bhimsen Joshi, both of the Kirana gharana.

The trap: (b) is tempting because Mansur first trained under Nilkanth Bua Alurmath of the Gwalior gharana, but he made his name in the Jaipur-Atrauli style he later learnt from Alladiya Khan's sons.

Read more: Nitin Singhania, Indian Art and Culture, on the gharanas of Hindustani music.

en.explanation:
Answer: (b) Atharvaveda. Its hymn 2.12 invokes kshetrasya patni, the 'mistress of the field'.

The Atharvaveda, the fourth Veda, is a later Vedic collection of charms and prayers for daily life: healing, protection, prosperity and farming, closer to popular belief than the Rigveda's hymns to the great gods. The Rigveda (hymn 4.57) already praises a male 'lord of the field', kshetrapati; the female 'mistress of the field' first appears in the Atharvaveda.

The trap: (a) is tempting because the Rigveda praises a 'lord of the field' (kshetrapati, hymn 4.57), but the female 'mistress of the field' appears first in the Atharvaveda.

en.text:
Consider the following statements with reference to India’s response to climate change:
I. India’s Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategy (LT-LEDS) is a crucial tool for achieving net-zero emissions by 2070.
II. India’s 4th Biennial Update Report (BUR-4) submitted in December, 2024 recorded around 8% decrease in Greenhouse gas emissions in 2020 over 2019.
III. Climate-resilient development necessarily depends on quick and short-term achievement of emission reduction targets.
Which of the following relationships among the above statements is/are correct?
1. Statement I is empirically supported by statement II.
2. Statement III contradicts the approach implicit in statement I.
3. Statement I and statement III together establish the premise of long-term sustainability.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (b) 1 and 2. BUR-4's emissions data backs the long-term LT-LEDS path, and Statement III's short-term view runs against it.

  • Statement I: correct. BUR-4, submitted on 30 December 2024, shows 2020 emissions 7.93% below 2019 and the emission intensity of GDP down 36% since 2005, data in line with the low-emission path the LT-LEDS sets.
  • Statement II: correct. The LT-LEDS charts a gradual, decades-long move to net zero by 2070 that protects development needs; insisting on quick, short-term cuts runs against that approach.
  • Statement III: incorrect. Statement III clashes with Statement I and is itself flawed, since resilience does not hinge on quick short-term cuts; the two cannot jointly found a premise of long-term sustainability.

India's climate commitments work at three levels: the net-zero by 2070 target announced at COP26 in Glasgow (2021); the Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategy, submitted at COP27 in Sharm el-Sheikh (November 2022), which charts the path; and reports to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), such as Biennial Update Reports, which track emissions. The approach is gradual and development-first, in line with common but differentiated responsibilities.

The trap: (c) is tempting because Statements I and III both concern climate action, but III's short-term focus contradicts I's long horizon, so the two cannot jointly set a premise of long-term sustainability.

Read more: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, India's Fourth Biennial Update Report to the UNFCCC (December 2024) and India's LT-LEDS (November 2022).

hi.text:
जलवायु परिवर्तन पर भारत की अनुक्रिया के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
I. भारत की दीर्घकालिक निम्न उत्सर्जन विकास रणनीति (LT-LEDS), वर्ष 2070 तक नेट-जीरो उत्सर्जन को प्राप्त करने के लिए एक निर्णायक साधन है।
II. दिसंबर, 2024 में प्रस्तुत की गई भारत की चौथी द्विवार्षिक अद्यतन रिपोर्ट (BUR-4) में 2019 की तुलना में 2020 में ग्रीनहाउस गैस उत्सर्जनों में लगभग 8% कमी दर्ज की गई।
III. जलवायु-अनुकूल (क्लाइमेट-रेज़िलिएन्ट) विकास अनिवार्य रूप से उत्सर्जन न्यूनीकरण लक्ष्यों की त्वरित और अल्प-कालिक उपलब्धि पर निर्भर है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों के बीच के संबंधों में से निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा/कौन-से सही है/हैं?
1. कथन I, कथन II द्वारा आनुभविक रूप से समर्थित है।
2. कथन III, कथन I में निहित दृष्टिकोण का खंडन करता है।
3. कथन I और कथन III सम्मिलित रूप से दीर्घकालिक स्थिरता (sustainability) की आधारिका (premise) को स्थापित करते हैं।
नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर उत्तर चुनिए:

en.text:
With respect to the Western Hoolock Gibbons, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. A Sanctuary in North-east India is home to this ape species listed as Endangered in the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Red List.
2. They have specialized brachiation and can easily swing between trees.
3. They possess a strong and heavy build like gorillas, yet are remarkably agile tree climbers.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (b) 1 and 2. The Western Hoolock Gibbon is an Endangered, brachiating ape of North-east India, but it is small and light, not gorilla-like.

  • Statement 1: correct. The Hollongapar Gibbon Sanctuary in Jorhat district, Assam, protects this ape, which the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) lists as Endangered.
  • Statement 2: correct. Gibbons are specialist brachiators: with very long arms they swing hand over hand from branch to branch through the canopy.
  • Statement 3: incorrect. Hoolock gibbons are slender 'lesser apes' weighing about 6–9 kg; their light build, not a heavy gorilla-like one, is what makes their agility possible.

Hoolock gibbons are the only apes found in India. The Western Hoolock Gibbon lives in the forest canopy of North-east India, Bangladesh and Myanmar west of the Chindwin river, and is listed as Endangered by the IUCN. Gibbons are 'lesser apes', far smaller and lighter than great apes such as gorillas.

The trap: (c) is tempting because gibbons are apes like gorillas, but they are small, light 'lesser apes'; a heavy, gorilla-like build would make their swinging way of life impossible.

Read more: IUCN Red List of Threatened Species, assessment of the Western Hoolock Gibbon (Hoolock hoolock).

hi.text:
वेस्टर्न हूलॉक गिबनों के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा/कौन-से कथन सही है/हैं?
1. पूर्वोत्तर भारत में एक अभयारण्य इस वानर जाति (species) का घर है जिसे अंतर्राष्ट्रीय प्रकृति संरक्षण संघ (आई.यू.सी.एन.) की लाल सूची में लुप्तप्राय (Endangered) के रूप में सूचीबद्ध किया गया है।
2. उनके पास विशिष्ट बाहुगमन (ब्रैकिएशन) की क्षमता है और वे आसानी से पेड़ों के बीच झूल सकते हैं।
3. गोरिला की भाँति, वे मज़बूत और स्थूलकाय होते हैं, तथापि वे असाधारण रूप से फुर्तीले वृक्षारोही हैं।
नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर उत्तर चुनिए:

en.text:
Which of the following best explain(s) the rationale for protecting mangrove ecosystems in the context of climate resilience?
1. Mangroves reduce tidal energy and store freshwater, making them ideal sites for paddy cultivation in saline estuarine belts.
2. Their salt-sensitive roots filter seawater, making mangroves key to converting coastal land into freshwater aquaculture zones.
3. By withstanding tidal surges and offering biomass resources, mangroves function both as natural bio-shields and livelihood bases for rural communities.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (d) 3 only. Mangroves shield coasts from surges and support livelihoods; they are salt-tolerant, hold no fresh water, and are lost to aquaculture.

  • Statement 1: incorrect. Mangroves do damp tidal energy, but they grow in salty water and store no fresh water; clearing them for paddy removes the very coastal shield they provide.
  • Statement 2: incorrect. Mangrove roots are salt-tolerant, not salt-sensitive, and turning mangrove land into aquaculture ponds is a leading cause of mangrove loss.
  • Statement 3: correct. Mangrove belts absorb wave and surge energy and yield fish, crabs, honey and fuelwood; in the 1999 Odisha super cyclone, villages behind wider mangroves suffered fewer deaths.

Mangroves are salt-tolerant trees of the tidal zone of tropical coasts and estuaries, with stilt roots and breathing roots (pneumatophores). They protect coasts from storms and erosion, trap sediment, store large amounts of carbon and serve as nurseries for fish. India's largest mangrove forest is the Sundarbans, and the MISHTI scheme (2023) promotes new mangrove planting along the coast.

The trap: (a) is tempting because mangroves do slow tides, but they grow in salt water and hold no fresh water; turning them into paddy fields would destroy the bio-shield the question is about.

Read more: Forest Survey of India, India State of Forest Report 2023, chapter on mangrove cover.

hi.text:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा/कौन-से, जलवायु अनुकूलन (climate resilience) के संदर्भ में गरान (मैंग्रोव) पारिस्थितिकी तंत्रों के संरक्षण हेतु तर्काधार की सर्वोत्तम व्याख्या करता है/करते हैं?
1. गरान ज्वारीय ऊर्जा को कम करते हैं और अलवणजल का संचयन करते हैं, जो उन्हें लवणीय ज्वारनदमुखी कटिबंधों में धान की खेती के लिए आदर्श स्थल बनाते हैं।
2. उनकी लवण-संवेदी जड़ें समुद्रीजल को छानती हैं, इस प्रकार तटीय भूमि को अलवण जलीय कृषि (एक्वाकल्चर) क्षेत्रों में परिवर्तित करने में गरानों की मुख्य भूमिका होती है।
3. ज्वारीय लहरों (टाइडल सर्जेस) को सहन करने तथा जैवमात्रा (बायोमास) संसाधनों को उपलब्ध करवाने के माध्यम से, गरान प्राकृतिक जैव-ढाल (बायोशील्ड) और ग्रामीण समुदायों के लिए जीविका के आधार, दोनों रूपों में कार्य करते हैं।
नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर उत्तर चुनिए:

en.text:
In what way(s) does the Vizhinjam International Seaport represent a structural shift in India’s maritime trade and logistics policy?
1. By functioning exclusively as a domestic cargo hub to reduce reliance on coastal shipping and eliminate the need for foreign collaborations.
2. By focusing primarily on passenger cruise tourism and heritage shipping to increase Kerala’s profile as a maritime heritage destination.
3. By leveraging its natural deep draft and strategic location to reduce dependence on foreign trans-shipment ports, enhance revenue retention, and reposition India in regional maritime trade.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (d) 3 only. Vizhinjam is a deep-water transshipment hub meant to bring home cargo now handled at foreign ports such as Colombo.

  • Statement 1: incorrect. Vizhinjam is an international container transshipment port, developed by Adani Ports in partnership with the Kerala government to serve global mainline ships, not a domestic-only hub.
  • Statement 2: incorrect. The port is built for container transshipment; passenger cruises and heritage shipping are not its purpose.
  • Statement 3: correct. Its naturally deep water and position about 10 nautical miles from the main east–west shipping route let large ships transship in India rather than at Colombo or Singapore.

Transshipment means moving containers from one ship to another at a hub port. Lacking a deep-water hub, India had about three-quarters of its transshipment cargo handled at foreign ports such as Colombo and Singapore, losing revenue. Vizhinjam, near Thiruvananthapuram, India's first deep-water container transshipment port, was dedicated to the nation on 2 May 2025.

The trap: (a) is tempting because the port aims to cut reliance on foreign hubs, but it does so as an international transshipment hub built with a private operator, not as a domestic-only port.

Read more: Press Information Bureau (PIB) release of 2 May 2025 on the dedication of Vizhinjam International Seaport to the nation.

hi.text:
विझिनजाम अंतर्राष्ट्रीय समुद्री पत्तन, भारत के समुद्री व्यापार और संभार तंत्र (लॉजिस्टिक्स) नीति में संरचनात्मक परिवर्तन को किस रूप/किन रूपों में निरूपित करता है?
1. तटीय पोत परिवहन पर निर्भरता को कम करने और विदेशी सहयोग की आवश्यकता को समाप्त करने के लिए केवल एक घरेलू कार्गो केंद्र के रूप में कार्य करना।
2. मुख्यतः यात्री क्रूज पर्यटन और विरासत पोत परिवहन पर केंद्रित करते हुए एक समुद्री विरासत गंतव्य के रूप में केरल की पहचान (प्रोफाइल) को बढ़ाना।
3. अपनी प्राकृतिक गहराई (डीप ड्राफ्ट) और रणनीतिक अवस्थान का लाभ उठाते हुए विदेशी यानांतरण (ट्रांस-शिपमेंट) पत्तनों पर निर्भरता को कम करना, राजस्व बनाए रखने को बढ़ाना, और क्षेत्रीय समुद्री व्यापार में भारत को पुनः स्थापित करना।
नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर उत्तर चुनिए:

en.text:
Identify the river of the Indian sub-continent on the basis of the following information:
1. It has an antecedent drainage system.
2. It flows through three countries.
3. It originates in the Tibetan Plateau and is an important river for irrigation.
4. It does not form distributaries.
Select the answer from the following:
en.explanation:
Answer: (c) Sutlej. It rises in Tibet, cuts through the Himalaya as an antecedent river, crosses China, India and Pakistan, and joins the Chenab without forming distributaries.

An antecedent river is older than the mountains it crosses: it kept cutting down as the Himalaya rose, carving deep gorges, as the Indus, Sutlej and Brahmaputra did. The Sutlej rises at Rakas Tal near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet, where it is called Langchen Khambab, enters India at Shipki La, feeds the Bhakra Nangal canals, and in Pakistan merges with the Chenab before the combined stream joins the Indus.

The trap: (b) is tempting because the Indus is also antecedent, rises in Tibet and crosses three countries, but it ends in a delta of many distributaries in Sindh; the Brahmaputra too ends in a delta, shared with the Ganga.

Read more: NCERT Class 11, India: Physical Environment, chapter Drainage System, on the Indus system and its tributaries.

2. यह तीन देशों में से होकर बहती है।
3. इसका उद्गम तिब्बत के पठार में होता है और यह सिंचाई के लिए महत्त्वपूर्ण नदी है।
4. इसकी कोई वितरिका नहीं है।

en.text:
Which of the following with reference to Indian States is/are not correct?
1. Uttar Pradesh shares its boundary with the highest number of other Indian States.
2. Rajasthan shares the longest international border among all Indian States.
3. Sikkim is the only State that shares its boundary with just one other Indian State.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (c) 2 and 3. West Bengal, not Rajasthan, has the longest international border, and Meghalaya, like Sikkim, touches only one other State.

  • Statement 1: correct. Uttar Pradesh touches eight States (Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and Bihar) plus Delhi, more than any other State.
  • Statement 2: incorrect. West Bengal has the longest international border: its border with Bangladesh alone is about 2,217 km, roughly twice Rajasthan's border with Pakistan, and it also borders Nepal and Bhutan.
  • Statement 3: incorrect. Meghalaya also touches only one State, Assam, with Bangladesh on its other side, so Sikkim, which touches only West Bengal, is not the only such State.

Questions on State boundaries test counts that are easy to check on a map. Uttar Pradesh touches the most States, eight, and Assam touches seven. Sikkim (West Bengal) and Meghalaya (Assam) each touch just one. West Bengal has the longest international border, with Bangladesh, Nepal and Bhutan, and the 4,096.7 km Bangladesh border is India's longest with any country.

The trap: (d) is tempting because Rajasthan's long desert border with Pakistan is well known, but West Bengal's border with Bangladesh alone is about twice as long, so statement 2 is also not correct.

Read more: Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), Annual Report, chapter on Border Management, for the length of each land border and the States along it.

hi.text:
भारतीय राज्यों के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा/कौन-से सही नहीं है/हैं?
1. उत्तर प्रदेश सबसे अधिक संख्या में अन्य भारतीय राज्यों के साथ अपनी सीमा साझा करता है।
2. सभी भारतीय राज्यों में से राजस्थान सबसे लंबी अंतर्राष्ट्रीय सीमा साझा करता है।
3. सिक्किम एकमात्र राज्य है जो केवल एक अन्य भारतीय राज्य के साथ अपनी सीमा साझा करता है।
नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर उत्तर चुनिए:

en.text:
Which of the following statements with regard to the arrival of Amur Falcons at Doyang Lake in Nagaland each year from Mongolia is/are correct?
1. It showcases how sustained local conservation efforts can contribute to the arrival and protection of international migratory birds.
2. It reflects the global success of advanced tracking technologies that guide migratory birds back to their stopover sites.
3. It confirms that Amur Falcons have adapted to permanent residency in India due to favourable habitat changes.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (a) 1 only. The falcons' safe stopover at Doyang is a community conservation success; they are passage migrants, not residents.

  • Statement 1: correct. After mass trapping of the falcons at the Doyang reservoir in Wokha district came to light in 2012, villagers of nearby Pangti banned the hunt and now guard the roost, called the Falcon Capital of the World.
  • Statement 2: incorrect. Satellite tags fitted to a few falcons only record their routes for scientists; they do not guide the birds, which find their way on their own.
  • Statement 3: incorrect. Amur falcons stop in Nagaland only for a few weeks in October and November to feed, then cross the Arabian Sea to winter in southern Africa, and return to East Asia to breed.

The Amur falcon breeds in south-eastern Siberia, northern China and Mongolia and winters in southern Africa, a yearly round trip of over 20,000 km that includes a non-stop crossing of the Arabian Sea, one of the longest migrations of any bird of prey. North-east India, above all the Doyang reservoir in Nagaland, is its main stopover. Its protection there shows how a local community can safeguard an international migrant.

The trap: (b) is tempting because satellite tracking of Amur falcons often makes news, but the tags only record where the birds fly; they do not guide them to their stopover sites.

Read more: BirdLife International, species factsheet for the Amur Falcon (Falco amurensis).

hi.text:
मंगोलिया से प्रत्येक वर्ष नागालैंड के दोयंग झील में अमूर बाज़ों (Amur Falcons) के आगमन के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा/कौन-से कथन सही है/हैं?
1. यह दर्शाता है कि कैसे निरंतर स्थानीय संरक्षण प्रयास अंतर्राष्ट्रीय प्रवासी पक्षियों के आगमन और संरक्षण में योगदान दे सकते हैं।
2. यह उन उन्नत ट्रैकिंग प्रौद्योगिकियों की वैश्विक सफलता को दर्शाता है जो प्रवासी पक्षियों को अपने प्रवास स्थल (स्टॉपओवर साइट) पर वापस जाने का मार्ग दिखाती हैं।
3. यह पुष्टि करता है कि अमूर बाज़ों ने अनुकूल आवास संबंधी परिवर्तनों के कारण भारत को स्थायी निवास स्थल (रेजिडेन्सी) के रूप में अपना लिया है।
नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर उत्तर चुनिए:

en.text:
Which among the following is/are the objective(s) of the Rainfed Area Development (RAD) initiative under the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA)?
1. Encouraging monoculture in rainfed areas
2. Increasing rice cultivation in irrigated regions
3. Enhancing productivity and minimising climatic risks through Integrated Farming Systems (IFS)
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (d) 3 only. RAD builds Integrated Farming Systems in rainfed areas; it moves farmers away from monoculture and does not target irrigated rice.

  • Item 1: no. RAD promotes diversification, joining crops with horticulture, livestock, fisheries, agro-forestry and bee-keeping, to move rainfed farmers away from risky single-crop farming.
  • Item 2: no. RAD works in rainfed areas and builds diversified farming systems there; raising rice output in irrigated regions is not among its aims.
  • Item 3: yes. RAD's stated focus is Integrated Farming Systems (IFS) for enhancing productivity and minimising risks from climatic variability, so income from allied activities cushions a crop failure.

The National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA), one of the eight missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC), was operationalised in 2014-15 to make farming productive and climate-resilient. Its Rainfed Area Development (RAD) component takes an area-based approach, combining crops with livestock, horticulture, fisheries and agro-forestry, so farmers have income to fall back on when drought or flood damages a crop.

The trap: (c) is tempting because rice is India's main food crop, but RAD works in rainfed areas and promotes integrated, diversified farming; irrigated rice is outside its scope.

Read more: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Operational Guidelines of the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA).

en.text:
Which of the following is/are the most significant implication(s) of obtaining Oeko-Tex certification for Eri Silk in the global textile industry?
1. It allows Indian exporters to compete in high-end markets that prioritise chemical-free products.
2. It confirms that Eri Silk meets international safety, environmental, and quality standards, enabling its entry into premium eco-conscious markets.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (c) Both 1 and 2. The certificate shows Eri silk is tested free of harmful substances, which opens premium, eco-conscious markets abroad.

  • Statement 1: correct. Oeko-Tex testing checks textiles for harmful substances such as heavy metals, formaldehyde and banned azo dyes, so certified Eri silk can compete in high-end markets that want chemical-free products.
  • Statement 2: correct. The certification, obtained in August 2024 by the North Eastern Handicrafts and Handlooms Development Corporation (NEHHDC), assures foreign buyers that the silk meets international safety and quality standards.

Eri silk, made mostly in Assam and the rest of the North-east from the castor-fed silkworm Philosamia ricini, is called ahimsa or peace silk because it is spun from cocoons after the moth has left them. In August 2024 the NEHHDC, under the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (DoNER), obtained Oeko-Tex certification for it. Oeko-Tex, run by an association of independent textile testing institutes, labels textiles tested for harmful substances, a mark that premium buyers look for.

The trap: (a) is tempting because statement 1 names a concrete market gain, but statement 2 is the basis of that gain: the certificate itself tells buyers the silk meets international safety and quality standards.

Read more: PIB, Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region, August 2024 release on Oeko-Tex certification for Eri silk.

en.text:
Ships from which of the following countries have to cross the Strait of Hormuz to reach out to the Indian Ocean?
1. Bahrain
2. Syria
3. Qatar
4. Egypt
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (b) 1 and 3. Bahrain and Qatar lie inside the Persian Gulf, whose only outlet to the open ocean is the Strait of Hormuz.

  • Item 1: yes. Bahrain is an island state inside the Persian Gulf, so every ship leaving it must pass the Strait of Hormuz to reach the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea.
  • Item 2: no. Syria's only coast is on the Mediterranean; its ships reach the Indian Ocean through the Suez Canal, the Red Sea and the Bab-el-Mandeb strait.
  • Item 3: yes. Qatar is a peninsula jutting into the Persian Gulf with no other coast, so its ships, including its large liquefied natural gas (LNG) exports, must sail out through Hormuz.
  • Item 4: no. Egypt has coasts on the Mediterranean and the Red Sea; its ships reach the Indian Ocean through the Red Sea and Bab-el-Mandeb, far from Hormuz.

The Strait of Hormuz, between Iran to the north and Oman's Musandam peninsula to the south, is the only sea link between the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea. Iraq, Kuwait, Bahrain and Qatar depend on it entirely; Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Iran also have coasts outside the Gulf. About a fifth of the world's oil supply passes through it, so tension there moves oil prices.

The trap: (d) is tempting because Egypt sits on a key shipping route, but its route to the Indian Ocean runs through the Suez Canal, Red Sea and Bab-el-Mandeb, not through Hormuz.

en.text: Tungurahua Volcano, which was declared a Global Geopark by UNESCO in 2025, is situated in which one among the following countries?
en.explanation:
Answer: (a) Ecuador. Tungurahua is an active volcano in Ecuador's Andes, and its geopark was among 16 new UNESCO Global Geoparks named in April 2025.

Tungurahua is an active stratovolcano about 5,000 m high in the Andes of central Ecuador, near the spa town of Banos, and it erupted repeatedly from 1999 to the mid-2010s. Ecuador lies on the Pacific Ring of Fire, where the Nazca Plate dives under the South American Plate. UNESCO Global Geoparks are areas of international geological value managed for conservation, education and sustainable tourism.

The trap: (b) is tempting because Peru shares the same Andean volcanic belt, with volcanoes such as El Misti, but Tungurahua stands in central Ecuador, near Banos.

en.text:
With reference to Madhav National Park, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It was declared a Tiger Reserve in India in 2025.
2. Sakhya Sagar, which is designated as a Ramsar Site, is situated within this National Park.
3. Its area is shared between Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (b) 1 and 2. Madhav became India's 58th tiger reserve in March 2025 and holds the Sakhya Sagar Ramsar site; it lies wholly in Madhya Pradesh.

  • Statement 1: correct. Madhav National Park in Shivpuri district was declared India's 58th tiger reserve, and Madhya Pradesh's ninth, in March 2025, after tigers were brought back to it from 2023.
  • Statement 2: correct. Sakhya Sagar, a man-made lake inside the park on the edge of Shivpuri town, was listed as a Ramsar site, a wetland of international importance, in 2022.
  • Statement 3: incorrect. The park lies wholly in Shivpuri district of Madhya Pradesh, in the upper Vindhyan hills; no part of it is in Rajasthan.

Tiger reserves are notified by State governments on the advice of the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. Madhav, once a royal hunting ground of the Scindias of Gwalior, became the 58th in March 2025, three months after Ratapani, also in Madhya Pradesh, the State with the most tigers. A Ramsar site is a wetland listed under the 1971 Ramsar Convention.

The trap: (a) is tempting if Sakhya Sagar is unfamiliar, but this lake inside the park became one of Madhya Pradesh's Ramsar sites in 2022.

Read more: National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA), list of tiger reserves of India.

en.text:
With reference to the climate of Andaman and Nicobar Islands, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. The climate can be defined as a humid, tropical coastal climate.
2. It receives rainfall from both South-west monsoon and North-east monsoon.
3. Maximum precipitation is between December and May.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (b) 1 and 2. The islands have a humid tropical coastal climate with rain from both monsoons; the wettest months run from May to December.

  • Statement 1: correct. Lying in the tropics and surrounded by sea, the islands stay warm and humid all year with little change in temperature, a humid tropical coastal climate.
  • Statement 2: correct. The south-west monsoon reaches the islands in May, earlier than the mainland, and the north-east monsoon brings more rain in November and December.
  • Statement 3: incorrect. Most rain falls between May and December, from the two monsoons; January to April is the islands' dry season.

The Andaman and Nicobar Islands get about 3,000 mm of rain a year. The south-west monsoon arrives in May, before it reaches Kerala, and the north-east monsoon adds rain in November and December, so the wet season runs from May to December, with the south-west monsoon giving the larger share. Being small islands in the tropics, they have high humidity and a very small annual range of temperature.

The trap: (c) is tempting because the islands do get north-east monsoon rain late in the year, but the heaviest rain comes with the south-west monsoon from May, and January to April is dry.

Read more: Andaman and Nicobar Administration, official website, page on the geography and climate of the islands.

en.text:
Which of the following geographical features or phenomena is/are associated with the Peninsular Block of India?
1. Submergence of parts of the western coast due to tectonic activity
2. Presence of residual mountain ranges such as the Veliconda hills and Mahendragiri hills
3. Deep, V-shaped river valleys formed by fast-flowing rivers
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (b) 1 and 2. A partly submerged western coast and residual hills belong to the old, rigid Peninsula; deep V-shaped valleys belong to the young Himalaya.

  • Item 1: yes. The Peninsula has stood as a rigid block since the Cambrian period, except for some of its western coast, which has been submerged beneath the sea, and a few other parts changed by tectonic activity.
  • Item 2: yes. The Peninsula consists mostly of relict and residual mountains such as the Aravali, Nallamala, Javadi and Veliconda hills, the Palkonda range and the Mahendragiri hills.
  • Item 3: no. Peninsular river valleys are shallow with low gradients; deep V-shaped valleys cut by fast rivers mark the young Himalaya.

By geological structure India has three divisions: the Peninsular Block, the Himalaya and other Peninsular mountains, and the Indo-Ganga-Brahmaputra Plain. The Peninsular Block, a part of ancient Gondwana land, is old and stable, worn down into residual hills and broad, shallow valleys. The Himalaya are young, weak and flexible, and their rivers, still in a youthful stage, cut deep gorges and V-shaped valleys.

The trap: (c) is tempting because the Peninsula is called rigid and stable, which seems to rule out submergence, but parts of its western coast did sink beneath the sea, while its valleys are shallow, not V-shaped.

Read more: NCERT Class 11, India: Physical Environment, Chapter 2, Structure and Physiography.

en.text:
Consider the following statements with reference to the Sagarmala Programme of the Government of India:
I. The Sagarmala Programme seeks to achieve port-led economic growth through cost-effective and sustainable coastal infrastructure.
II. The success of the Sagarmala Programme is reflected in significant growth in coastal and inland waterway shipping, along with improved global port rankings.
III. Sagarmala 2.0 aims to position India as a global maritime innovation hub aligned with Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat 2047 visions.
Which of the following relationships among the above statements is/are correct?
1. Statement II validates the effectiveness of the strategies envisioned in statement I.
2. Statement III extends the objectives of statement I by embedding them into a future-oriented innovation framework.
3. Statement I contradicts statement III by focusing only on traditional infrastructure instead of modern innovation.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (b) 1 and 2. Statement II reports results of the port-led strategy in I, and III carries that strategy forward; I and III do not contradict each other.

  • Statement I: correct. Statement II reports results, such as 118% growth in coastal shipping and 700% growth in inland waterway cargo over Sagarmala's first decade, that bear out the port-led strategy of Statement I.
  • Statement II: correct. Sagarmala 2.0 keeps the port-led growth aim of Statement I and adds shipbuilding, ship repair, recycling and support for maritime start-ups, tied to the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision.
  • Statement III: incorrect. Statement I sets out the programme's basic aim and Statement III builds on it, so the two are complementary; a newer phase widening an older aim does not contradict it.

The Sagarmala Programme of the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, approved in 2015, uses India's 7,500 km coastline and navigable waterways for port-led development through port modernisation, port connectivity, port-led industrialisation and coastal community development, cutting logistics costs. Marking its first decade in 2025, the government reported nine Indian ports among the world's top 100, and Sagarmala 2.0 widened the focus to shipbuilding, repair and recycling.

The trap: (c) is tempting because Statement I speaks of infrastructure while III speaks of innovation, but a later phase that widens an earlier aim extends it rather than contradicting it.

Read more: PIB, Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, March 2025 release on ten years of the Sagarmala Programme.

3. आधुनिक नवाचार के स्थान पर केवल पारंपरिक अवसंरचना पर केंद्रित होने के कारण कथन I, कथन III का खंडन करता है।

en.text:
Consider the following statements about Rhynchostylis retusa (Foxtail orchid):
1. It is an epiphytic orchid.
2. The species is endemic to North-east India.
3. It is the State flower of Arunachal Pradesh and Assam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
en.explanation:
Answer: (b) 1 and 3. The foxtail orchid grows on trees and is the State flower of Arunachal Pradesh and Assam, but it is found well beyond the North-east.

  • Statement 1: correct. It grows on the trunks of trees, taking moisture from air and rain without feeding on its host, and hangs dense sprays of flowers shaped like a fox's tail.
  • Statement 2: incorrect. It is native across South and South-east Asia, from India, Nepal and Sri Lanka to Myanmar, Thailand, Indonesia and the Philippines, so it is not endemic to North-east India.
  • Statement 3: correct. It is the State flower of Arunachal Pradesh and of Assam, where it is called kopou and is worn in the hair by women dancing Bihu.

Epiphytes grow on other plants for support but make their own food, unlike parasites; many orchids, ferns and mosses are epiphytes. A species is endemic only if it is found naturally in one region and nowhere else, and many orchids of North-east India also grow in neighbouring countries. The foxtail orchid is a cultural symbol in Assam, tied to Rongali Bihu, and a State symbol in Arunachal Pradesh.

The trap: (c) is tempting because the foxtail orchid is so closely tied to Assam and Arunachal Pradesh, but it grows wild across South and South-east Asia, so it is not endemic to the North-east.

Read more: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, Plants of the World Online, entry for Rhynchostylis retusa, on its native range.

en.text:
Which one of the following statements with regard to the Moidams, built by the Tai-Ahom kingdom and inscribed as a World Heritage Site by UNESCO, is/are correct?
1. They acted as army fortresses.
2. They were recreation centres of the Royals and Nobles.
3. They were burial grounds of the Royals and Nobles.
4. They were battle drill centres of the Royals and Nobles.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (c) 3 only. Moidams are earthen burial mounds of Ahom kings, queens and nobles, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2024.

  • Statement 1: incorrect. Moidams are funerary mounds raised over vaulted burial chambers and had no military use; they were never army fortresses.
  • Statement 2: incorrect. Moidams were sacred tombs, not places of leisure; the Ahom pavilion from which royals watched games and sports was the Rang Ghar at Sivasagar.
  • Statement 3: correct. Moidams are mound burials: the dead, with goods for the afterlife, were placed in a vault of brick, stone or earth under an earthen mound, and Charaideo holds those of Ahom royals and nobles.
  • Statement 4: incorrect. No moidam served as a drill or training ground; the Charaideo mounds were sacred burial sites kept for royal funerary rites.

The Ahom dynasty, founded by Chaolung Sukaphaa in 1228, ruled the Brahmaputra valley for about 600 years, and Charaideo was its first capital. Its kings, queens and nobles were buried in moidams, vaults under earthen mounds. In July 2024, at the 46th session of the World Heritage Committee in New Delhi, Moidams, the Mound-Burial System of the Ahom Dynasty, became India's 43rd World Heritage Site and the first cultural one in the North-east.

The trap: (b) is tempting because it includes the burial statement, but moidams were never army fortresses; they served only as tombs of royals and nobles.

Read more: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Moidams, the Mound-Burial System of the Ahom Dynasty (inscribed 2024).

en.text:
At the United Nations Ocean Conference (UNOC) held in June, 2025 in France, the Food and Agricultural Organization (FAO) of the United Nations demonstrated its leading voice on marine and ocean issues, especially on sustainable fisheries and aquaculture for resilient livelihood and “Blue Transformation”.
Which of the following combinations about the “Four Betters” proposed by FAO for “Blue Transformation” is correct?
options: Better production, better nutrition, better environment and better ocean
Better production, better nutrition, better environment and better life
Better coral reefs, better nutrition, better environment and better life
Better estuaries, better nutrition, better environment and better mangrove vegetation
en.explanation:
Answer: (b) Better production, better nutrition, better environment and better life. These four betters frame FAO's Strategic Framework 2022–31, under which Blue Transformation sits.

The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) Strategic Framework 2022–31 aims at more efficient, inclusive, resilient and sustainable agrifood systems for better production, better nutrition, a better environment and a better life, leaving no one behind. Blue Transformation, FAO's roadmap for aquatic food systems, is a programme priority area under better production. The third UN Ocean Conference, co-hosted by France and Costa Rica, met at Nice in June 2025.

The trap: (a) is tempting because the conference was about oceans, but the fourth better is better life; the four betters are FAO's aims for all agrifood systems, not ocean-specific goals.

en.text:
Which of the following statements with reference to Lake Turkana is/are correct?
1. It is the largest desert lake in the world.
2. The lake is situated in South Sudan along the eastern fringe of the Sahara desert.
3. The lake is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is also referred to as the ‘Jade Sea’.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (b) 1 and 3 only. Lake Turkana, the Jade Sea, is the world's largest desert lake and a World Heritage Site; it lies in Kenya's Rift Valley, not in South Sudan.

  • Statement 1: correct. Lake Turkana, in the hot, arid north of Kenya, is the world's largest permanent desert lake and also the world's largest alkaline lake.
  • Statement 2: incorrect. It lies in the Rift Valley of northern Kenya, with its northern tip in Ethiopia; it is not in South Sudan, and its dry basin is part of East Africa, not the Sahara.
  • Statement 3: correct. The Lake Turkana National Parks became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997, and the lake's striking blue-green colour has earned it the name Jade Sea.

Lake Turkana, once called Lake Rudolf, gets most of its water from the Omo River of Ethiopia and has no outlet, so it is saline. Its national parks, Sibiloi, Central Island and South Island, form a World Heritage Site also known for fossils of early humans at Koobi Fora. The site was put on the List of World Heritage in Danger in 2018 over the effects of Ethiopia's Gibe III dam on the Omo.

The trap: (d) is tempting because the lake lies in a hot desert region of Africa, but it is in Kenya's Rift Valley, with its northern tip in Ethiopia, not in South Sudan on the Sahara's fringe.

Read more: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Lake Turkana National Parks (Kenya), inscribed 1997, extended 2001.

en.text:
Which of the following statements with regard to genetic medicine is/are correct?
1. Genetic medicines correct/compensate for the faulty genes responsible for disease.
2. Engineered viruses and lipid nanoparticles are used as carriers of the genetic medicine.
3. Genetic medicines alter the entire DNA sequence.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (c) 1 and 2 only. Genetic medicines fix, replace or offset a faulty gene and are carried into cells by viral vectors or lipid nanoparticles; they do not rewrite all of the DNA.

  • Statement 1: correct. Genetic medicines treat disease at its source by repairing or replacing a faulty gene, adding a working copy, or silencing a harmful one, as in gene therapies for haemophilia and sickle cell disease.
  • Statement 2: correct. Engineered, disabled viruses such as adeno-associated virus (AAV) and lentivirus, and fat-based lipid nanoparticles like those in mRNA vaccines, carry the genetic material into cells.
  • Statement 3: incorrect. They act on one target gene or its RNA message; even gene editing such as CRISPR changes a small, chosen stretch of DNA, never the whole sequence.

Genetic medicine covers gene therapy (adding or replacing a gene), gene editing (changing a gene in place, as with CRISPR-Cas9) and RNA medicines (mRNA, siRNA and antisense) that change which proteins a cell makes. Getting the material into the right cells is the main challenge, which is why viral vectors and lipid nanoparticles matter. India approved its first home-grown CAR-T cell therapy, NexCAR19, in 2023.

The trap: (d) is tempting because gene editing sounds like rewriting the genome, but genetic medicines target a specific faulty gene; they never alter the entire DNA sequence.

Read more: NCERT Class 12 Biology, chapter Biotechnology and its Applications, section on gene therapy.

en.text:
Which of the following statements with regard to Large Language Models (LLMs) used in machine learning is/are correct?
1. LLMs assign probabilities to the next possible words and then pick the one with the highest probability.
2. LLMs process data through mathematical optimization to minimise prediction errors.
3. LLMs produce unbiased outputs.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (b) 1 and 2 only. LLMs predict the next word from learned probabilities and are trained to minimise prediction error; they absorb biases from their data.

  • Statement 1: correct. An LLM turns its input into a probability for every possible next token (a word or part of a word) and, in the basic greedy method, outputs the most likely one, repeating this word by word.
  • Statement 2: correct. Training adjusts the model's billions of parameters by gradient descent to minimise a loss function, the error between its predicted next word and the actual word in the training text.
  • Statement 3: incorrect. LLMs learn from vast human-written text and so absorb its social, cultural and gender biases; they can also state false things confidently, so their output is not unbiased.

A large language model is a neural network, usually of the transformer type, trained on huge amounts of text to predict the next token. In use, it computes a probability for each possible next token and chooses one, the most likely in greedy decoding or a sampled one when a temperature setting allows variety. Because it mirrors its training data, it can repeat biases and produce confident errors (hallucinations), so fine-tuning and human oversight are needed.

The trap: (d) is tempting because LLMs are mathematical systems that seem neutral, but they learn from human text and carry its biases, so statement 3 is wrong.

Read more: NITI Aayog, Responsible AI for All, Approach Document Part 1 (2021), on bias and other risks of AI systems.

en.text:
Which of the following statements with regard to stealth technology is/are correct?
1. Stealth objects have a very small radar cross-section and are coated with Radar Absorbing Material.
2. Stealth objects can be detected using specific frequencies.
3. Stealth objects are coated with metamaterials to increase the scattering of electromagnetic radiation.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (c) 1 and 2 only. Stealth shrinks the radar echo with shaping and absorbent coatings, yet some radar frequencies can still detect it.

  • Statement 1: correct. Stealth aircraft and ships are shaped to deflect radar waves away from the source and coated with Radar Absorbing Material (RAM) that turns radar energy into heat, giving a very small radar cross-section (RCS).
  • Statement 2: correct. Stealth shaping and coatings work best against high-frequency fire-control radars; low-frequency (VHF and UHF) radars, whose long waves match the size of aircraft parts, can still detect stealth aircraft, if less precisely.
  • Statement 3: incorrect. Metamaterial coatings are designed to absorb radar waves or bend them around the object so that less energy returns to the radar; the aim is to cut the radar echo, not to increase scattering.

An object's radar cross-section (RCS) measures how much radar energy it reflects back towards the radar. Stealth lowers it through shaping (angled flat surfaces, hidden engine inlets, internal weapons bays), radar-absorbing materials and, increasingly, metamaterials. Stealth means low observability, not invisibility: low-frequency, passive and multistatic radars and infrared sensors can still pick up stealth platforms.

The trap: (d) is tempting because metamaterials are a real stealth technology, but they are meant to absorb radar waves or bend them around the object, cutting the echo, not to increase scattering.

Read more: Encyclopaedia Britannica, article on stealth (military technology).

en.text:
Which of the following statements with regard to Black Boxes used in modern aircrafts is/are correct?
1. They carry a beacon emitting red light pulses to facilitate underwater detection.
2. They record both the cockpit voice and flight data.
3. Their memory units are made using either stainless steel or titanium.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (b) 2 and 3 only. Black boxes record cockpit sound and flight data inside a steel or titanium memory unit; their underwater beacon sends sound pulses, not light.

  • Statement 1: incorrect. The underwater locator beacon, which switches on when immersed, sends ultrasonic sound pulses (pings) at 37.5 kHz, not light; sound travels far through water, light does not.
  • Statement 2: correct. An airliner carries a cockpit voice recorder (CVR) for crew speech and cockpit sounds and a flight data recorder (FDR) for readings such as altitude, speed and heading; some aircraft combine the two in one unit.
  • Statement 3: correct. The data sits in a crash-survivable memory unit whose armoured shell is made of stainless steel or titanium, over thermal insulation, to withstand impact, fire and deep-water pressure.

Despite the name, flight recorders are painted bright orange to be easy to find. Their memory is built to survive severe impact, fire and long submersion, and their beacon pings for at least 30 days, with newer rules requiring 90. Black boxes were in the news after the Air India Flight 171 crash at Ahmedabad on 12 June 2025, when investigators recovered the recorders to find out what went wrong.

The trap: (d) is tempting because black boxes do carry a locator beacon, but it emits ultrasonic sound pulses, since light does not travel far underwater, so statement 1 is wrong.

Read more: International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), Annex 6 to the Chicago Convention (Operation of Aircraft), provisions on flight recorders.

en.text:
Which of the following statements with regard to Green Hydrogen is/are correct?
1. It is decarbonized hydrogen obtained from natural gas reforming combined with carbon capture and storage (CCS).
2. It is produced using electrolysis of water with electricity generated by renewable energy.
3. National Green Hydrogen Mission of India aims for abatement of nearly 50 MMT of annual greenhouse gas emissions by 2030.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (b) 2 and 3 only. Green hydrogen comes from splitting water with renewable power; hydrogen from natural gas with carbon capture is blue hydrogen.

  • Statement 1: incorrect. Hydrogen from natural gas reforming with carbon capture and storage (CCS) is called blue hydrogen, and without capture it is grey; green hydrogen uses no fossil fuel at all.
  • Statement 2: correct. Green hydrogen is made by splitting water into hydrogen and oxygen in an electrolyser powered by renewable electricity such as solar or wind, so its production emits almost no carbon dioxide.
  • Statement 3: correct. The National Green Hydrogen Mission, approved in January 2023 with an outlay of Rs 19,744 crore, targets 5 million tonnes of green hydrogen a year by 2030 and abatement of nearly 50 MMT of annual greenhouse gas emissions.

Hydrogen is colour-coded by how it is made: grey from natural gas without capturing the carbon, blue from natural gas with carbon capture and storage, and green from electrolysis of water using renewable power. India's Green Hydrogen Standard (2023) treats hydrogen as green if its well-to-gate emissions are at most 2 kg of carbon dioxide equivalent per kg of hydrogen, whether made by electrolysis or from biomass. The mission's SIGHT programme supports electrolyser manufacturing and green hydrogen production.

The trap: (d) is tempting because hydrogen from natural gas with carbon capture is also low-carbon, but that is blue hydrogen; only renewable-powered routes such as electrolysis give green hydrogen.

Read more: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), National Green Hydrogen Mission document (January 2023).
