en.text:
Consider the following statements with regard to involvement of private entities in India’s space programme:
1. The Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) is an autonomous agency formed to facilitate participation of private entities.
2. Agnikul Cosmos launched the world’s first flight using 3D-printed rocket engine.
3. Skyroot Aerospace has developed liquid fuel for GSLV.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
en.explanation:
Answer: (c) 1 and 2 only. IN-SPACe opens space activities to private firms and Agnikul flew a rocket on a 3D-printed engine; Skyroot builds its own Vikram rockets, not GSLV fuel.

  • Statement 1: correct. The Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe), set up in 2020 under the Department of Space, is an autonomous single-window agency that promotes, authorises and supervises private space activities.
  • Statement 2: correct. On 30 May 2024 Agnikul Cosmos flew Agnibaan SOrTeD from its own launch pad at Sriharikota, powered by Agnilet, billed as the world's first single-piece 3D-printed rocket engine, a semi-cryogenic one.
  • Statement 3: incorrect. Skyroot Aerospace builds its own Vikram rockets (Vikram-S, in November 2022, was the first privately built Indian rocket to fly); GSLV and its propellants are ISRO's own.

The 2020 space sector reforms opened India's space programme to private firms, with IN-SPACe, headquartered in Ahmedabad, as promoter and authoriser, NewSpace India Limited (NSIL) as the commercial arm of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), and the Indian Space Policy 2023 setting out the roles. Two start-ups lead in launch vehicles: Skyroot Aerospace of Hyderabad with its Vikram series, and Agnikul Cosmos of Chennai, incubated at IIT Madras, with Agnibaan.

The trap: (d) is tempting because Skyroot is India's best-known private rocket maker, but it develops its own Vikram launch vehicles; it has not made fuel for ISRO's GSLV.

A note: Rocket Lab's Electron has flown on largely 3D-printed Rutherford engines since 2017, so statement 2 is strictly true only of a single-piece 3D-printed engine, which is how Agnikul described its 2024 flight.

Read more: Department of Space, Indian Space Policy 2023, on the roles of IN-SPACe, NSIL and private entities.

3. स्काईरूट एयरोस्पेस ने GSLV के लिए तरल ईंधन (Liquid fuel) विकसित किया।

en.text:
Which of the following statements with regard to drone swarms is/are correct?
1. They use Terahertz band of frequency to communicate with the command centre.
2. Individual drones in the swarm can communicate with other drones in the swarm.
3. GPS Spoofing is a commonly used technique to counter drone swarm attack.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (b) 2 and 3 only. Swarm drones talk to each other to act together, and GPS spoofing is a common counter; they do not depend on the terahertz band.

  • Statement 1: incorrect. Drones and swarms link to their controllers over ordinary radio bands such as 2.4 GHz and 5.8 GHz, or over satellite and cellular links; terahertz links are short-range and still experimental.
  • Statement 2: correct. Drones in a swarm share position and task data over drone-to-drone (mesh) links, so the group can coordinate, avoid collisions and carry on even if some drones are lost.
  • Statement 3: correct. Counter-drone systems commonly jam or spoof satellite navigation signals; spoofing feeds false GPS positions to steer drones off course or force them to land.

A drone swarm is a group of drones that coordinate through on-board software and inter-drone links, often using artificial intelligence, to act as one system, so losing a few drones does not stop the mission. Counter-drone measures are soft kill (radio jamming, Global Positioning System (GPS) jamming and spoofing, cyber takeover) or hard kill (guns, missiles, lasers and other directed-energy weapons). Cheap swarms can overwhelm costly air defences.

The trap: (d) is tempting because terahertz waves are studied for future 6G links, but today's drones and swarms communicate over ordinary radio bands such as 2.4 and 5.8 GHz, so statement 1 is wrong.

Read more: Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO), its D4 anti-drone system (detect, deter and destroy).

en.text:
Which of the following statements with regard to GenomeIndia Project is/are correct?
1. It is a part of the Human Genome Project.
2. The project is funded by the Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Government of India.
3. Its primary aim is to build a catalogue of genetic diversity of the Indian population.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (b) 2 and 3 only. GenomeIndia is India's own DBT-funded project to map the genetic variety of Indians; it is not part of the Human Genome Project.

  • Statement 1: incorrect. The Human Genome Project was an international effort of 1990–2003 that produced the first human reference genome; GenomeIndia, begun in 2020, is a separate Indian project.
  • Statement 2: correct. It is funded by the Department of Biotechnology (DBT) under the Ministry of Science and Technology and carried out by a consortium of about 20 Indian research institutions.
  • Statement 3: correct. Its main aim is a catalogue of genetic variation among Indians; in January 2025 it released the genomes of about 10,000 people from many population groups, held at the Indian Biological Data Centre (IBDC).

Reference genomes built mostly from people of European descent miss much of the genetic variety of India's many population groups. GenomeIndia fills this gap, helping to find disease-linked variants, predict responses to drugs and develop personalised medicine. Its data, stored at the IBDC in Faridabad, is shared with researchers under the Framework for Exchange of Data Protocols (FeED), with samples anonymised.

The trap: (d) is tempting because GenomeIndia also sequences human genomes, but the Human Genome Project ended in 2003; GenomeIndia is a separate national project run by DBT.

Read more: PIB, Ministry of Science and Technology, January 2025 release on the GenomeIndia data of 10,000 genomes.

en.text:
Which of the following statements with regard to the National Quantum Mission (NQM) is/are correct?
1. It aims at developing intermediate-scale quantum computers with 50 – 1000 physical qubits.
2. Its implementation includes setting up of four Thematic Hubs (T-Hubs) in academic and national R&D institutes across India.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (c) Both 1 and 2. The mission targets quantum computers of 50–1000 physical qubits within eight years and works through four Thematic Hubs.

  • Statement 1: correct. Approved in April 2023 with an outlay of about Rs 6,003 crore for 2023-24 to 2030-31, the mission aims at intermediate-scale quantum computers with 50–1000 physical qubits in eight years, on platforms such as superconducting and photonic.
  • Statement 2: correct. Four Thematic Hubs (T-Hubs) host its work: quantum computing at IISc Bengaluru, communication at IIT Madras with C-DOT, sensing and metrology at IIT Bombay, and materials and devices at IIT Delhi.

The National Quantum Mission (NQM), run by the Department of Science and Technology (DST), aims to seed and scale quantum research and industry in India. Besides quantum computers, it targets satellite-based secure quantum communication between ground stations over 2,000 km, inter-city quantum key distribution, high-sensitivity magnetometers and atomic clocks. A qubit can be 0 and 1 at once (superposition), which lets quantum computers tackle certain problems far faster.

The trap: (a) is tempting if the hub structure is unfamiliar, but the mission is built around four T-Hubs, one each for computing, communication, sensing and metrology, and materials and devices.

Read more: PIB, Union Cabinet decision of 19 April 2023 approving the National Quantum Mission.

en.text:
Which of the following statements with regard to India’s Deep Ocean Mission is/are correct?
1. It was launched by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Government of India.
2. Matsya-6000 has been designed to carry 3 people for deep sea exploration.
3. Samudrayaan is a project under this mission.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (b) 2 and 3 only. The Deep Ocean Mission belongs to the Ministry of Earth Sciences; Samudrayaan, its crewed dive project, uses the three-person Matsya-6000.

  • Statement 1: incorrect. The Deep Ocean Mission is a programme of the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES), approved by the Union Cabinet in June 2021 at a cost of about Rs 4,077 crore over five years.
  • Statement 2: correct. Matsya-6000, built by the National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT), Chennai, is a crewed submersible designed to take three people to 6,000 m depth in a titanium alloy sphere.
  • Statement 3: correct. Samudrayaan, India's first crewed deep-ocean mission, is the Deep Ocean Mission's project to send scientists to 6,000 m in Matsya-6000.

The Deep Ocean Mission supports India's Blue Economy aims. Its components include deep-sea mining technology and the crewed submersible, ocean climate change advisory services, deep-sea biodiversity, exploration of deep-sea minerals such as hydrothermal sulphides, energy and fresh water from the ocean, and a marine biology station. With Samudrayaan, India seeks to join the few countries with deep-diving crewed submersibles, such as the US, Russia, France, Japan and China.

The trap: (c) is tempting because an ocean mission sounds like a ports and shipping matter, but the Deep Ocean Mission belongs to the Ministry of Earth Sciences, which handles ocean science.

Read more: PIB, Union Cabinet approval of the Deep Ocean Mission, 16 June 2021.

en.text:
Mr. X, a senior officer, was overseeing a critical vaccination programme during a pandemic. He found that a private service provider responsible for vaccine distribution was compromising on quality to make profits. Despite immense pressure to manage the issue due to vested interests, he raised his voice based on the principles of public administration which he learnt during various training programmes attended across his career. He reported the issue to the appropriate vigilance authority and halted the contract to ensure citizen welfare.
Which one among the following principles of public administration was most strongly demonstrated by Mr. X’s actions?
en.explanation:
Answer: (c) Accountability. Mr. X answered for public money and citizens' safety by reporting the lapse to the vigilance authority and halting the contract.

Accountability means a public servant must answer for how public power, money and trust are used, and must act when that trust is betrayed, even under pressure from vested interests. Esprit de corps (team spirit) and equity (fair and kind treatment of staff) are among Henri Fayol's 14 principles of management, and delegation is the passing of authority to subordinates; none of them describes reporting a contractor's wrongdoing to the vigilance authority.

The trap: (b) is tempting because Mr. X acted for citizens' welfare, but equity means fair and even-handed treatment; reporting the contractor to the vigilance authority and halting the contract is answering for a public duty, which is accountability.

Read more: Second Administrative Reforms Commission, Fourth Report, Ethics in Governance (2007).

hi.text:
श्री X, एक वरिष्ठ अधिकारी हैं, जो किसी विश्वमारी के दौरान एक निर्णायक टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम का निरीक्षण कर रहे थे। उन्होंने पाया कि टीके के वितरण के लिए उत्तरदायी एक निजी सेवा प्रदाता, लाभ अर्जित करने के लिए गुणवत्ता से समझौता कर रहा है। निहित स्वार्थों के कारण, इस मामले को निपटाने हेतु अत्यधिक दबाव होने के बावजूद, अपने जीविका (कैरिअर) के विविध प्रशिक्षण कार्यक्रमों में भागीदारी के दौरान सीखे गए लोक प्रशासन के सिद्धांतों के आधार पर उन्होंने अपनी आवाज़ उठाई। उन्होंने इस मामले को समुचित सतर्कता प्राधिकारी को प्रतिवेदित किया और नागरिकों के कल्याण को सुनिश्चित करने के लिए उस संविदा को रोक दिया।
श्री X की कार्रवाई से लोक प्रशासन के निम्नलिखित सिद्धांतों में से कौन-सा सर्वाधिक प्रभावी रूप से प्रदर्शित होता है?

en.text:
In a multi-ethnic district where both economic competition and historical grievances frequently led to community tensions, a flashpoint has arisen with a Government decision to allocate land for a waste management facility near a tribal hamlet, sparking protests by the tribal community, which claimed that the land was sacred and critical to their cultural identity. At the same time, urban residents and local industries supported the project, citing severe solid waste challenges and health concerns due to lack of a proper disposal site. The conflict has escalated with road blockades, social media campaigns, and allegations of police excesses.
As a responsible Government official, you are tasked with resolving the situation through mediation, ensuring a sustainable outcome that balances environmental needs, tribal rights, and urban public health.
Consider the following statements with reference to the above:
1. A successful conflict resolution process must begin with acknowledging the cultural concerns of the protesting tribal community before discussing technical alternatives.
2. The Government should move ahead with the project without delay to address urban health concerns, which outweigh the sentiments of a small group.
3. Creating a multi-stakeholder dialogue platform — including tribal leaders, environmental experts, and municipal representatives — to build mutual understanding and help de-escalate tensions.
4. Conducting an independent Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and sharing findings transparently with both sides to facilitate evidence-based decision-making.
Which of the statements given above would contribute to the resolution process?
en.explanation:
Answer: (a) 1, 3 and 4 only. Acknowledging concerns, dialogue and an open impact study help resolve the conflict; forcing the project through does not.

  • Statement 1: correct. Acknowledging that the tribal community holds the land sacred builds trust; people who feel heard are more willing to discuss other sites or designs.
  • Statement 2: incorrect. Pushing the project through and dismissing the tribal community as a small group would harden the protests and ignore their protected rights; it escalates the conflict instead of resolving it.
  • Statement 3: correct. A platform that brings tribal leaders, environmental experts and municipal representatives together lets each side hear the other directly, which lowers tension and opens room for compromise.
  • Statement 4: correct. An independent Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA), shared openly with both sides, puts verified facts on the table, so the decision rests on evidence rather than suspicion.

Mediation in a conflict between a development need and community rights rests on recognition, participation and transparency: acknowledge the hurt party's concerns, bring all stakeholders to one table, and base the decision on independent evidence shared openly. A solution imposed in the name of a majority need, however real, leaves the conflict unresolved and can override the rights of tribal communities.

The trap: (d) is tempting because the urban health problem is real and urgent, but statement 2 asks the Government to override the tribal community without dialogue, which would escalate the protests rather than resolve them.

Read more: Second Administrative Reforms Commission, Seventh Report, Capacity Building for Conflict Resolution (2008).

hi.text:
एक बहुजातीय ज़िले में, जहाँ आर्थिक प्रतिस्पर्धा और ऐतिहासिक शिकायतों के परिणामस्वरूप प्रायः सामुदायिक तनाव उत्पन्न होते हैं, वहाँ एक जनजातीय उपग्राम के निकट एक अपशिष्ट प्रबंधन सुविधा-केंद्र के लिए भूमि आबंटित करने संबंधी एक सरकारी निर्णय से एक चिंगारी निकली और जनजातीय समुदाय का विरोध भड़क उठा, जिसमें दावा किया गया है कि यह भूमि उनकी सांस्कृतिक पहचान के लिए पवित्र और महत्त्वपूर्ण है। उसी समय, शहरी निवासी और स्थानीय उद्योग समूह एक उपयुक्त निपटान स्थल के न होने के कारण उत्पन्न ठोस अपशिष्ट की गंभीर चुनौतियों और स्वास्थ्य चिंताओं का हवाला देते हुए इस परियोजना का समर्थन करते हैं। यह संघर्ष सड़क अवरोध, सोशल मीडिया अभियानों, और पुलिस के अतिरेक के आरोपों के चलते तीव्र हो गया।
एक ज़िम्मेदार सरकारी अधिकारी के रूप में, आपको मध्यस्थता के माध्यम से इस स्थिति का समाधान करने एवं पर्यावरणीय आवश्यकताओं, जनजाति के अधिकारों, और शहरी जन-स्वास्थ्य के बीच संतुलन बनाते हुए एक संधारणीय परिणाम सुनिश्चित करने का कार्य सौंपा गया है।
उपर्युक्त के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
1. तकनीकी विकल्पों पर चर्चा करने से पहले, विरोध करने वाले जनजाति समुदाय की सांस्कृतिक चिंताओं को स्वीकार करने के साथ ही, एक सफल संघर्ष समाधान प्रक्रिया अवश्य आरंभ की जानी चाहिए।
2. शहरी स्वास्थ्य चिंताओं के समाधान के लिए, सरकार को अविलंब परियोजना को आगे बढ़ाना चाहिए, जो कि किसी लघु वर्ग की भावनाओं से कहीं अधिक महत्त्वपूर्ण है।
3. पारस्परिक समझ विकसित करने और तनावों को कम करने में सहायता के लिए जनजाति नेताओं, पर्यावरण विशेषज्ञों, और नगर पालिका के प्रतिनिधियों को सम्मिलित करते हुए एक बहु-हितधारक संवाद मंच का गठन करना।
4. साक्ष्य-आधारित निर्णयन को सुकर बनाने के लिए एक स्वतंत्र पर्यावरणीय और सामाजिक प्रभाव मूल्यांकन (ESIA) को संचालित करना और प्राप्त निष्कर्षों को दोनों पक्षों के साथ पारदर्शी रूप से साझा करना।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से, इस समाधान प्रक्रिया में योगदान देंगे?

subtopic.title: Civil services, administrative reform and ethics

en.text:
Ms. X is a mid-level civil service official working in the urban development department of a major city. Recently, she was involved in approving a contract for a public infrastructure project — a new community park. During the approval process, she received a piece of confidential information indicating that one of the shortlisted contractors had a history of poor workmanship and allegations of corruption in other cities, though nothing had been legally proven. The Head of the Department, Mr. Y, advised her not to disclose this information to the project committee or the public because it could delay the project and damage the city’s reputation. However, Ms. X believed that withholding such information compromised transparency and public trust.
What amongst the following should Ms. X do now?
1. Immediately disclose the information to the project committee and the public
2. Recommend removing the contractor from the shortlist to protect the project’s integrity
3. Propose a ‘limited disclosure’ to an oversight committee, while keeping the information confidential from the public for the time being
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (b) 3 only. Telling an oversight committee lets the concern be checked through proper channels without damaging a contractor over unproven claims.

  • Item 1: no. The allegations are unproven and the information is confidential; announcing them publicly could unfairly damage the contractor and breach the duty to keep official information confidential.
  • Item 2: no. Dropping a contractor on allegations that were never proven denies due process; any exclusion must follow the procurement rules after a proper inquiry, and Ms. X cannot decide it alone.
  • Item 3: yes. Limited disclosure to an oversight committee lets a competent body verify the record before the contract is awarded, keeping the process transparent without harming anyone on unproven claims.

Transparency and confidentiality have to be balanced. A civil servant who learns of a risk to public money should neither hide it, as Mr. Y advised, nor broadcast unverified claims; the right course is to place it before the body competent to examine it. Due process, meaning action only after verification, is part of fairness in public procurement.

The trap: (c) is tempting because removing a contractor with a poor record seems to protect the project, but the allegations were never proven; removing the contractor without an inquiry would be arbitrary, so only the limited disclosure fits.

Read more: Second Administrative Reforms Commission, First Report, Right to Information: Master Key to Good Governance (2006).

hi.text:
सुश्री X, एक मध्यम-स्तरीय सिविल सेवा अधिकारी हैं, जो एक प्रमुख नगर के शहरी विकास विभाग में कार्यरत हैं। हाल ही में, वे एक सार्वजनिक अवसंरचना परियोजना — नए सामुदायिक उद्यान हेतु संविदा की अनुमोदन प्रक्रिया में सम्मिलित थीं। अनुमोदन प्रक्रिया के दौरान, उन्हें एक गोपनीय सूचना प्राप्त होती है, जिसमें इसका उल्लेख है कि चयनित सूची में सम्मिलित एक संविदाकार के अन्य नगरों में घटिया कार्य-शैली और भ्रष्टाचार के आरोपों का पूर्ववृत्त रहा है, यद्यपि विधि द्वारा कुछ भी प्रमाणित नहीं हुआ है। विभागाध्यक्ष श्री Y, उन्हें इस सूचना को परियोजना समिति अथवा जनता के समक्ष प्रकट न करने की सलाह देते हैं, क्योंकि इससे परियोजना में विलंब हो सकता है और नगर की प्रतिष्ठा को हानि हो सकती है। हालाँकि, सुश्री X का मानना है कि ऐसी सूचना को रोकना, पारदर्शिता और जनता के विश्वास से समझौता करना होगा।

en.text:
‘X’ was addressing a seminar on the meaning of the term ‘law’ as provided under Article 13, Part III of the Constitution of India. ‘X’ explained that the meaning of the term ‘law’ in the Constitution of India was very comprehensive. It included ordinances, orders and even rules and regulations. ‘Y’ pointed out that the term ‘law’ in Article 13 also included custom or usage having in the territory of India the force of law, to which ‘X’ was not convinced.
Based on the above, select the correct conclusion from the options given below:
options: ‘X’ is correct in the interpretation of law, including the view on non-inclusion of custom.
The view of ‘Y’ that ‘law’ included custom is not correct.
The views of both ‘X’ and ‘Y’ are correct.
The view of only ‘Y’ is correct.
en.explanation:
Answer: (d) The view of only ‘Y’ is correct. Article 13(3)(a) expressly includes custom or usage having the force of law.

Article 13 makes void any law that is inconsistent with, or takes away or abridges, the Fundamental Rights. Article 13(3)(a) defines 'law' widely: any Ordinance, order, bye-law, rule, regulation, notification, custom or usage having in the territory of India the force of law. So even a custom can be struck down for violating Fundamental Rights. Article 13(4), added by the 24th Amendment (1971), keeps constitutional amendments made under Article 368 out of this definition.

The trap: (c) is tempting because X's list of ordinances, orders, rules and regulations is accurate, but X rejected custom, the very point in dispute, and Article 13(3)(a) names custom or usage expressly, so only Y's view holds.

Read more: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity, chapter on Fundamental Rights, section on laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights (Article 13).

‘Y’ का यह विचार कि ‘विधि’ में रूढ़ि सम्मिलित है, सही नहीं है।
‘X’ और ‘Y’ दोनों के विचार सही हैं।

en.text:
Consider the following statements with reference to the Constitution of India:
1. There is no Article in the Constitution of India that specifies that the Constitution of India will be officially called the ‘Constitution of India’.
2. There is no Article in the Constitution of India that specifies that the Indian Independence Act, 1947 and the Government of India Act, 1935 stand repealed.
3. There is no Article in the Constitution of India that mentions 26th January, 1950 as the date of the commencement of the Constitution of India.
Which one of the following conclusions based on the above statements is correct?
options: There are two correct statements that include statement 3.
There is only one correct statement.
en.explanation:
Answer: (b) There is no correct statement. Articles 393, 394 and 395 deal with all three points.

  • Statement 1: incorrect. Article 393, titled Short title, says that this Constitution may be called the Constitution of India.
  • Statement 2: incorrect. Article 395 repeals the Indian Independence Act, 1947 and the Government of India Act, 1935, with the Acts amending or supplementing the latter, but not the Abolition of Privy Council Jurisdiction Act, 1949.
  • Statement 3: incorrect. Article 394 brings the remaining provisions into force on 26 January 1950 and calls that day the commencement of this Constitution.

Part XXII (Articles 393 to 395) closes the Constitution: Article 393 gives its short title, Article 394 fixes its commencement and Article 395 repeals the two Acts of the British Parliament. Some provisions, such as citizenship (Articles 5 to 9) and elections (Article 324), came into force on 26 November 1949, the day of adoption; the rest began on 26 January 1950. Article 394A, added by the 58th Amendment (1987), deals with the authoritative Hindi text.

The trap: (c) is tempting for anyone who knows only that Article 395 repealed the two Acts, but Article 393 names the Constitution and Article 394 fixes 26 January 1950, so statements 1 and 3 are false too.

Read more: The Constitution of India, Part XXII, Articles 393 to 395 (Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice).

en.text:
Which of the following statements with regard to the persons with disabilities in India is/are correct?
1. The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, an Act passed by the Parliament of India in 2018, mandates reservation in education and employment, places a legal duty on Governments to ensure accessibility and non-discrimination.
2. The Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan focuses on achieving universal accessibility for Persons with Disabilities across three key domains — built infrastructure, transport systems and information and communication technology.
3. The National Divyangjan Finance and Development Corporation (NDFDC) is a public sector organisation set up by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs as a not-for-profit company to promote entrepreneurship among Persons with Disabilities (PwDs).
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (b) 2 only. The disability rights law dates from 2016, and NDFDC was set up by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

  • Statement 1: incorrect. The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act was enacted in December 2016 and came into force in April 2017, not 2018, though it does mandate reservation, accessibility and non-discrimination.
  • Statement 2: correct. The Accessible India Campaign (Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan), launched on 3 December 2015, targets three areas: the built environment, the transport system and the information and communication technology ecosystem.
  • Statement 3: incorrect. NDFDC, formerly the National Handicapped Finance and Development Corporation, was set up in 1997 by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, not the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 replaced the 1995 Act and raised the recognised disabilities from 7 to 21. Persons with benchmark disabilities (40 per cent or more) get 4 per cent reservation in government posts and at least 5 per cent of seats in government and aided higher education. The Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, runs the Accessible India Campaign and oversees NDFDC, a not-for-profit company that lends to persons with disabilities.

The trap: (a) is tempting because statement 1 describes the Act's duties correctly, but it gives the wrong year: the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act was enacted in 2016, not 2018.

Read more: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (depwd.gov.in), pages on the RPwD Act, 2016 and the Accessible India Campaign.

en.text:
Consider the following statements about the provisions pertaining to the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes in India:
1. Provisions regarding the administration of the Tribal Areas in the States of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram are given in the Fifth Schedule of the Constitution of India.
2. Some tribes of India are entitled to exemption from paying Income Tax on certain incomes.
3. The Constitution of India provides for reservation of seats in Panchayats for women belonging to the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes.
Which one of the following conclusions based on the above statements is correct?
options: There are two correct statements, that include statement 2.
There are two correct statements, that are statements 1 and 3.
There is only one correct statement.
en.explanation:
Answer: (a) There are two correct statements, that include statement 2. Statements 2 and 3 hold; statement 1 names the wrong Schedule.

  • Statement 1: incorrect. The tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram are governed by the Sixth Schedule (Article 244(2)); the Fifth Schedule covers Scheduled Areas in other States.
  • Statement 2: correct. Members of Scheduled Tribes living in specified north-eastern areas and Ladakh pay no income tax on income from sources there (Section 10(26) of the Income-tax Act, 1961, carried into the 2025 Act).
  • Statement 3: correct. Article 243D(2) reserves at least one-third of the Panchayat seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes for women of those communities.

Article 244 splits tribal administration: the Fifth Schedule covers Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in States other than Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram (Scheduled Areas exist in ten States), with a Tribes Advisory Council and special powers for the Governor, while the Sixth Schedule sets up autonomous district councils in those four States. Article 243D reserves Panchayat seats for SCs and STs in proportion to their population, with one-third of these for women of those groups.

The trap: (d) is tempting because the four north-eastern States do have special tribal provisions, but those are in the Sixth Schedule, not the Fifth, so statement 1 is false.

Read more: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity, chapter on Scheduled and Tribal Areas.

en.text:
Consider the following statements in respect of questions asked by the Members in the Parliament of India:
1. Unstarred questions are those to which a Member desires an oral answer in the House.
2. Starred questions are those to which a Member desires a written answer.
3. No supplementary question can be asked on an unstarred question.
Which one of the following conclusions based on the above statements is correct?
options: All the three statements are correct.
There are two correct statements, that include statement 2.
There is only one correct statement.
en.explanation:
Answer: (c) There is only one correct statement. Only statement 3 holds; statements 1 and 2 swap starred and unstarred questions.

  • Statement 1: incorrect. An unstarred question gets a written answer, laid on the Table of the House; it is the starred question that is answered orally.
  • Statement 2: incorrect. A starred question, marked with an asterisk, is one the Member wants answered orally on the floor of the House.
  • Statement 3: correct. An unstarred question is answered in writing, so no supplementary question can follow it; supplementaries are allowed only on starred questions.

Question Hour, the first hour of a sitting in the Lok Sabha, uses three kinds of questions. Starred questions, marked with an asterisk, are answered orally and allow supplementary questions; unstarred questions get written answers and allow none; short notice questions, asked at less than ten days' notice on urgent matters, are answered orally. Zero Hour, which follows Question Hour, is an Indian innovation not mentioned in the rules.

The trap: (b) is tempting if the two kinds are swapped, which makes statements 1 and 2 look true, but a starred question gets an oral answer and an unstarred one a written reply.

Read more: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity, chapter on Parliament, section on Question Hour.

en.text:
Consider the following statements about the Committee on the Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes of the Parliament of India:
1. Although members of this Committee are elected from both Houses of Parliament, the Chairperson of this Committee is appointed by the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
2. Twenty members are elected by the Rajya Sabha and ten members by the Lok Sabha.
3. No Minister, except for the Union Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, is eligible to be a member of this Committee.
4. Members are elected for a fixed term of two years from the date they enter their office.
Which one of the following conclusions based on the above statements is correct?
options: There is only one correct statement, that is statement 2.
There are two correct statements, that include statement 1.
en.explanation:
Answer: (d) There is no correct statement. All four details about the Committee are wrong.

  • Statement 1: incorrect. The Chairperson is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha from among the Committee's members, not by the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
  • Statement 2: incorrect. The numbers are reversed: of the 30 members, 20 are elected by the Lok Sabha and 10 by the Rajya Sabha.
  • Statement 3: incorrect. No Minister of any ministry can be a member of the Committee; a member who becomes a Minister ceases to be a member.
  • Statement 4: incorrect. Members serve a term not exceeding one year and the Committee is reconstituted every year, so there is no fixed two-year term.

The Committee on the Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, first set up in 1968, has 30 members, 20 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha, elected by proportional representation by single transferable vote for terms of up to one year. It considers the reports of the National Commissions for SCs and for STs and examines how the Union carries out the safeguards for these communities. Like the financial committees, it keeps Ministers out.

The trap: (b) is tempting because 20 and 10 are the right numbers, but they are reversed: the Lok Sabha elects 20 members and the Rajya Sabha 10.

Read more: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity, chapter on Parliamentary Committees.

en.text:
Consider the following statements about Mission Sudarshan Chakra of India:
1. It aims to enhance India’s air defence, ballistic missile defence and aerial offensive capabilities.
2. This Mission is being designed to enhance rapid, precise, and powerful defence responses, reinforcing India’s strategic autonomy.
3. One of the aims of this Mission is to cover all public places of India by an expanded nationwide security shield by 2035.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
en.explanation:
Answer: (a) 1, 2 and 3. All three match the mission as the Prime Minister announced it on 15 August 2025.

  • Statement 1: correct. The mission is planned as a layered shield that joins air defence and ballistic missile defence with precision strike; the Prime Minister said it would also hit back at the enemy.
  • Statement 2: correct. The Prime Minister's Office described it as designed to enhance rapid, precise and powerful defence responses, reinforcing India's strategic autonomy, with the whole system to be built in India.
  • Statement 3: correct. The Prime Minister said all public places, strategic and civilian, such as hospitals, railways and centres of faith, would be covered by an expanded nationwide security shield by 2035.

Mission Sudarshan Chakra, announced in the Independence Day speech from the Red Fort on 15 August 2025, aims to build by 2035 an indigenous, multi-layered national security shield. It is meant to detect and neutralise threats from aircraft, missiles and drones and also to strike back, protecting strategic and civilian sites alike. Research, design and manufacture of the whole system are to be done in India.

The trap: (c) is tempting because a security shield sounds purely defensive, but the mission pairs defence with offence: the Prime Minister said it would neutralise the enemy's attack and also hit back many times over.

Read more: Prime Minister's Office, Independence Day address from the Red Fort, 15 August 2025 (pmindia.gov.in).

Consider the following statements about river bridges connecting India with neighbouring countries:
1. ‘Maitri Setu’, built over Feni river, connects Ramgarh in India with Sabroom in Bangladesh.
2. Jhulaghat suspension bridge connects India with Myanmar.
3. Mechi bridge and its approaches connect Panitanki Bypass in India with Kakarvitta in Nepal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
en.explanation:
Answer: (d) 3 only. Statement 1 swaps the two towns and statement 2 names the wrong neighbour.

  • Statement 1: incorrect. Maitri Setu over the Feni river links Sabroom in Tripura, India with Ramgarh in Bangladesh; the statement reverses the two towns.
  • Statement 2: incorrect. The Jhulaghat suspension bridge spans the Kali (Mahakali) river between Pithoragarh district of Uttarakhand and Nepal, not Myanmar.
  • Statement 3: correct. The Mechi bridge and its approaches on NH 327B, a National Highways and Infrastructure Development Corporation (NHIDCL) project funded through an Asian Development Bank loan, link the Panitanki bypass in West Bengal with Kakarvitta in Nepal.

India's river bridges with its neighbours carry trade and serve the Neighbourhood First and Act East policies. Maitri Setu, inaugurated in March 2021, gives Tripura a road link towards Chittagong port in Bangladesh. The Kali (Mahakali) river forms much of the India–Nepal border along Uttarakhand, and the Mechi river forms part of the border between West Bengal and eastern Nepal; the Mechi bridge lies on Asian Highway 2.

The trap: (c) is tempting because Maitri Setu does cross the Feni river between India and Bangladesh, but Sabroom is the Indian town in Tripura and Ramgarh is in Bangladesh, the reverse of statement 1.

en.text:
Which of the following statements about a Zero First Information Report (Zero FIR) under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 is/are correct?
1. A Zero FIR can be lodged at a police station, even though the place of commission of a cognizable/non-cognizable offence is outside the territorial jurisdiction of that police station.
2. The Officer-in-Charge of the police station where a Zero FIR has been lodged may, with the permission of the competent authority, initiate a preliminary enquiry.
3. Under Zero FIR, it is obligatory for the informant to furnish information electronically.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (d) 2 only. A Zero FIR covers cognizable offences only, and giving information electronically is an option, not a duty.

  • Statement 1: incorrect. Section 173(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) lets information be given irrespective of where the offence was committed only for cognizable offences; non-cognizable cases go under Section 174.
  • Statement 2: correct. Section 173(3) lets the officer in charge, with prior permission of an officer not below Deputy Superintendent of Police, hold a preliminary enquiry within 14 days for offences punishable with 3 to under 7 years.
  • Statement 3: incorrect. Section 173(1) allows information to be given orally or by electronic communication; an electronic complaint must be signed by the informant within three days, but filing it electronically is a choice.

The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, in force since 1 July 2024, replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. Its Section 173 gives statutory backing to the Zero FIR: a police station must record information about a cognizable offence wherever it took place, and the case then goes to the station with jurisdiction. It also allows e-FIRs and a preliminary enquiry for offences punishable with three years or more but less than seven years.

The trap: (c) is tempting because a Zero FIR can indeed be lodged at any police station regardless of jurisdiction, but only for cognizable offences; statement 1 wrongly extends it to non-cognizable ones.

Read more: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, Sections 173 and 174 (Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice).

With reference to the organisations under the Government of India, consider the following details:

Sl. No.OrganisationFunctionControlling Union Ministry
1.Central Economic Intelligence Bureau (CEIB)To coordinate between various law enforcement agenciesMinistry of Home Affairs
2.Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO)To investigate complex corporate fraudsMinistry of Finance
3.Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)To preserve values in public life and ensure the health of the national economyMinistry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pension

In how many of the above rows are the given details correctly matched?
en.explanation:
Answer: (a) 1. Only the CBI row, the third, is correctly matched.

  • Row 1: incorrect. The Central Economic Intelligence Bureau (CEIB), set up in 1985 to coordinate the agencies fighting economic offences, works under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, not the Ministry of Home Affairs.
  • Row 2: incorrect. The Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) does investigate complex corporate frauds, but it works under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, with statutory status under Section 211 of the Companies Act, 2013.
  • Row 3: correct. The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) describes its role as preserving values in public life and ensuring the health of the national economy, and works under the Department of Personnel and Training of this Ministry.

Investigating agencies sit under the ministry whose laws they mainly enforce. The CEIB, under the Ministry of Finance, coordinates intelligence and enforcement on economic offences. The SFIO, set up in 2003 and made statutory by the Companies Act, 2013, belongs to the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. The CBI, set up in 1963 by a Home Ministry resolution and drawing its powers from the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946, is now under the Department of Personnel and Training.

The trap: (b) is tempting because the SFIO's work on frauds sounds like a Finance Ministry job, but the SFIO is under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and the CEIB is under Finance, so only the CBI row is correct.

Consider the following statements with respect to the AI Impact Summit, 2026 held in New Delhi:
1. The Summit’s intellectual framework was based on three foundational Sutras : People, Planning, and Progress.
2. The Preamble of the Summit stresses Democratising AI Resources, which acknowledges the Charter for Democratic Diffusion of AI as a binding framework to support locally relevant innovation and strengthen resilient AI ecosystems while respecting national laws.
3. The New Delhi Declaration on AI Impact was structured around seven Chakras (Pillars), which included Access for Social Empowerment, AI for Science, and Secure and Trusted AI.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
en.explanation:
Answer: (d) 3 only. The Sutras were People, Planet and Progress, and the Charter on AI diffusion is voluntary and non-binding.

  • Statement 1: incorrect. The Summit's three Sutras were People, Planet and Progress; Planning was not one of them.
  • Statement 2: incorrect. The Declaration took note of the Charter for the Democratic Diffusion of AI as a voluntary and non-binding framework, not a binding one.
  • Statement 3: correct. The New Delhi Declaration on AI Impact rests on seven Chakras, among them access for social empowerment, AI for science, and secure and trusted AI, alongside human capital and democratising AI resources.

India hosted the AI Impact Summit at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, in February 2026, the first of the global AI summits held in the Global South, after Bletchley Park (2023), Seoul (2024) and Paris (2025). It was organised around three Sutras, People, Planet and Progress, and seven Chakras, or pillars, and closed with the New Delhi Declaration on AI Impact, endorsed by more than 80 countries and international organisations.

The trap: (c) is tempting because democratising AI resources was indeed one of the Chakras, but the Charter for the Democratic Diffusion of AI was noted only as a voluntary, non-binding framework, so statement 2 fails on the word binding.

Read more: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) and PIB releases on the India AI Impact Summit and the New Delhi Declaration, February 2026.

en.text:
Which of the following connectivity projects is/are a part of cooperation between India and the ASEAN member countries?
1. Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project
2. IMT Trilateral Highway
3. Agartala-Akhaura Rail Line
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (a) 1 and 2. Both run into Myanmar, and the highway on to Thailand, both ASEAN members; the Akhaura line goes to Bangladesh.

  • Item 1: yes. The Kaladan project links Kolkata to Sittwe port in Myanmar by sea, then runs by the Kaladan river to Paletwa and by road to Mizoram; Myanmar is an ASEAN member.
  • Item 2: yes. The India–Myanmar–Thailand Trilateral Highway runs from Moreh in Manipur through Myanmar to Mae Sot in Thailand, linking India with two ASEAN members.
  • Item 3: no. The Agartala–Akhaura rail line links Tripura with Bangladesh, which is not an ASEAN member, so it is India–Bangladesh cooperation.

India's Act East Policy treats the North-East as its land bridge to Southeast Asia, and Myanmar, the only ASEAN member sharing a land border with India, is the gateway. The Kaladan project gives Mizoram a route to the sea through Myanmar, and the Trilateral Highway is planned to extend later to Laos, Cambodia and Vietnam. Bangladesh is not in ASEAN, so links such as the Agartala–Akhaura line, inaugurated in November 2023, are bilateral projects under the Neighbourhood First policy.

The trap: (c) is tempting because the Agartala–Akhaura line is a well-known North-East connectivity project, but it links India with Bangladesh, which is not an ASEAN member.

Read more: Ministry of External Affairs, brief on India–ASEAN relations and the Act East Policy (mea.gov.in).

en.explanation:
Answer: (a) 1 and 2. Both are licence-built in India; Akula-class submarines are built in Russia, and India only leased one.

  • Item 1: yes. Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) builds the Su-30 MKI under licence from Russia at its Nashik plant in Maharashtra.
  • Item 2: yes. Armoured Vehicles Nigam Limited (AVNL) makes the T-90 Mk-III tank under licence from Russia at the Heavy Vehicles Factory, Avadi, near Chennai.
  • Item 3: no. Akula-class nuclear attack submarines are built in Russia; India only leased one, INS Chakra, from 2012 to 2021.

Licence production lets India build foreign-designed platforms at home: the Su-30 MKI at HAL Nashik and the T-90 Bhishma tank at Avadi are the main cases. Nuclear-powered attack submarines are different: India has leased Russian boats, while its own nuclear submarines, the Arihant class ballistic missile submarines, are built at the Ship Building Centre in Visakhapatnam.

The trap: (b) is tempting because India has operated an Akula-class submarine, INS Chakra, but it was built in Russia and leased; only the Su-30 MKI and the T-90 are made in India.

  • Statement 1: incorrect. The Colombo Process, of 12 Asian countries of origin of migrant workers, takes decisions by consensus, but they are non-binding.
  • Statement 2: correct. The Abu Dhabi Dialogue, set up in 2008, is a voluntary, non-binding process of Asian countries of labour origin and destination on contractual labour mobility.
  • Statement 3: correct. The Global Forum grew out of a proposal by UN Secretary-General Kofi Annan at the UN High-Level Dialogue on International Migration and Development in 2006, and is state-led, voluntary and non-binding.

Consultative processes on migration build trust and share good practice without binding commitments. The Colombo Process (2003) brings together Asian countries that send workers abroad, India among them; the Abu Dhabi Dialogue (2008) adds the destination countries, mainly in the Gulf; and the Global Forum on Migration and Development (GFMD), first held in Brussels in 2007, is a global, state-led, informal process outside the UN.

The trap: (a) is tempting because the Colombo Process does take decisions by consensus, but like the other two it is non-binding, so no member is bound by them.

2. United Nations Children’s Fund
3. United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
4. International Labour Organisation

en.explanation:
Answer: (a) 1. Only the UNHCR has won the Nobel Peace Prize twice, in 1954 and 1981.

  • Statement 1: incorrect. The World Food Programme won the Nobel Peace Prize once, in 2020, for its efforts to combat hunger.
  • Statement 2: incorrect. The United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) won the Nobel Peace Prize once, in 1965.
  • Statement 3: correct. The Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) won the Nobel Peace Prize twice, in 1954 and 1981.
  • Statement 4: incorrect. The International Labour Organisation won the Nobel Peace Prize once, in 1969, its 50th anniversary year.

UN bodies and related organisations that have won the Nobel Peace Prize include the UNHCR (1954 and 1981), UNICEF (1965), the ILO (1969), UN peacekeeping forces (1988), the UN with Kofi Annan (2001), the IAEA with Mohamed ElBaradei (2005), the IPCC with Al Gore (2007), the OPCW (2013) and the WFP (2020). The International Committee of the Red Cross, which is not a UN body, has won it three times.

The trap: (b) is tempting because UNICEF and the WFP are both well-known laureates, but each has won once; the UNHCR is the only one of the four with two prizes.

3. The share of the Central funding for the Revamped RGSA is 100% for all States and Union Territories.

en.explanation:
Answer: (b) 2 only. The revamped scheme runs from 2022–23 to 2025–26, and States share the cost of its State components.

  • Statement 1: incorrect. The Union Cabinet approved the Revamped RGSA in April 2022 for 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2026, to end with the 15th Finance Commission period; it did not start in 2021.
  • Statement 2: correct. Its stated aim is to develop the governance capabilities of Panchayati Raj Institutions to deliver on the Sustainable Development Goals through inclusive local governance.

The Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA), a centrally sponsored scheme of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, began in 2018 and was revamped in 2022 with an outlay of 5,911 crore rupees. It trains elected Panchayat representatives and staff, and helps Panchayats localise the Sustainable Development Goals through nine themes, such as poverty-free, healthy and water-sufficient villages. Central components such as e-Panchayat and incentives to Panchayats are fully funded by the Centre.

The trap: (a) is tempting because the scheme ends on 31 March 2026 with the 15th Finance Commission period, which began in 2021, but the revamped scheme itself started on 1 April 2022.

3. Germany
4. Switzerland

Answer: (c) 2 and 3. Germany is a founding member and Poland joined in 2004; Belarus and Switzerland are outside the EU.

  • Item 1: no. Belarus has never applied to join the European Union; it is tied to Russia through the Union State and the Eurasian Economic Union.
  • Item 2: yes. Poland joined the European Union on 1 May 2004, in the enlargement that took in ten countries.
  • Item 3: yes. West Germany was one of the six founders of the European Economic Community under the Treaty of Rome (1957), and united Germany is a member of the European Union.
  • Item 4: no. Switzerland is not in the European Union; it belongs to the European Free Trade Association and the Schengen Area and deals with the EU through bilateral agreements.

The European Union has had 27 members since the United Kingdom left on 31 January 2020. Several European states stay outside it: Switzerland, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein make up the European Free Trade Association (EFTA), and the last three join the EU single market through the European Economic Area. Belarus, Russia's close ally, belongs to the Eurasian Economic Union instead.

The trap: (d) is tempting because Switzerland sits among EU states and is in the Schengen Area, but it has never joined the EU; Swiss voters even rejected the European Economic Area in 1992.

Which of the following statements in relation to NIRANTAR (National Institute for Research and Application of Natural Resources to Transform, Adapt and Build Resilience), a platform of institutions under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, is/are correct?
1. Ecosystem Survey and Analysis is a vertical under this platform, the lead institute of which is Botanical Survey of India, Kolkata.

3. Capacity Development Support is a vertical under this platform, the lead institute of which is Indian Institute of Forest Management, Bhopal.

en.explanation:
Answer: (b) 1 and 3 only. The Botanical Survey of India and IIFM Bhopal lead their verticals; the ecosystem-services vertical is led by ICFRE, Dehradun, not the Central Zoo Authority.

  • Statement 1: correct. The Ecosystem Survey and Analysis vertical, which also groups the Zoological Survey and Forest Survey of India, is led by the Botanical Survey of India (BSI), Kolkata.
  • Statement 2: incorrect. NIRANTAR names the Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education (ICFRE), Dehradun, as lead of this vertical; the Central Zoo Authority is only one of its member bodies.
  • Statement 3: correct. The Capacity Development Support vertical, for training and capacity building in forest and natural resource management, is led by the Indian Institute of Forest Management (IIFM), Bhopal.

NIRANTAR is a Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change platform that links the ministry's existing survey and research bodies without creating a new institution or adding staff. It has four verticals: Ecosystem Survey and Analysis (lead BSI, Kolkata), Research and Management of Ecosystem Service (lead ICFRE, Dehradun), Capacity Development Support (lead IIFM, Bhopal) and Climate Change Support (lead National Centre for Sustainable Coastal Management, Chennai).

The trap: (a) is tempting because the Central Zoo Authority does sit in the ecosystem-services vertical, with the Wildlife Institute of India and the National Tiger Conservation Authority, but that vertical's lead institute is ICFRE, Dehradun.

Which of the following statements about DHRUV64 is/are correct?
1. It is the third chip fabricated under the DIR-V Programme with an overall aim to enable the creation of microprocessors for India.
2. It is India’s first homegrown 1·0 GHz, 64-bit dual-core microprocessor.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (c) Both 1 and 2. DHRUV64, built by C-DAC and launched in December 2025, is the third DIR-V chip and India's first homegrown 1.0 GHz, 64-bit dual-core processor.

  • Statement 1: correct. After THEJAS32, fabricated at Silterra in Malaysia, and THEJAS64, made at the Semiconductor Laboratory (SCL), Mohali, DHRUV64 is the third chip fabricated under the Digital India RISC-V (DIR-V) Programme.
  • Statement 2: correct. The Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC) built it under the Microprocessor Development Programme as India's first homegrown 1.0 GHz, 64-bit dual-core microprocessor.

RISC-V is an open instruction set architecture with no licence fees, so Indian designers can build processors on it freely. The Digital India RISC-V (DIR-V) Programme, launched in April 2022 by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), backs a family of such chips: THEJAS32, THEJAS64 and DHRUV64 from C-DAC, with DHANUSH64 and DHANUSH64+ under development. Earlier indigenous processors include SHAKTI (IIT Madras), AJIT (IIT Bombay) and VIKRAM (ISRO and SCL).

The trap: (b) is tempting because 'third chip' seems to clash with 'India's first', but 'first' refers only to its class (1.0 GHz, 64-bit, dual-core); THEJAS32 and THEJAS64 came before it under DIR-V.

Read more: PIB backgrounder, DHRUV64: India's First 1.0 GHz, 64-bit dual-core Microprocessor, 15 December 2025.

en.text:
The Bureau of Indian Standard (BIS) recently introduced a national standard to test and assess bomb disposal system. Which of the following statements with regard to this system is/are correct?
1. The new standard is known as IS 19445 : 2025.
2. It will improve interoperability of equipment across agencies.
3. It was developed by TBRL, DRDO in collaboration with the 30th Central Scientific Research Institute, Russia.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (c) 1 and 2 only. IS 19445:2025 sets common tests for bomb disposal gear; it was drafted in India with DRDO's TBRL, not with a Russian institute.

  • Statement 1: correct. The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) brought out IS 19445:2025, Bomb Disposal Systems: Performance Evaluation and Requirements, in December 2025.
  • Statement 2: correct. By fixing common test methods and acceptance benchmarks for bomb blankets, bomb baskets and bomb inhibitors, it aims at uniform evaluation and interoperability of equipment across agencies.
  • Statement 3: incorrect. A BIS committee drafted it at the request of the Ministry of Home Affairs and DRDO's Terminal Ballistics Research Laboratory (TBRL), Chandigarh, with Indian agencies such as the NSG; no Russian institute took part.

BIS, the national standards body under the Department of Consumer Affairs, framed IS 19445:2025 because international standards for bomb disposal equipment were hard to access or did not fit Indian threats and conditions. It lays down how bomb blankets, bomb baskets and bomb inhibitors are tested in the open for blast mitigation and for stopping fragments. TBRL convened the drafting panel, with inputs from the NSG, central armed police forces, state police and manufacturers.

The trap: (a) is tempting because defence standards sometimes draw on foreign expertise, but this one was developed in India by a BIS committee convened by TBRL with Indian security agencies and manufacturers.

Read more: Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), IS 19445:2025, Bomb Disposal Systems: Performance Evaluation and Requirements, released in December 2025.

Which of the following statements with regard to the Grand Slam Tennis Tournaments is/are correct?
1. The tournaments have a shared governance structure establishing the partnership among the four Grand Slam tournaments.
2. They are open for entry to all internationally ranked tennis players above the age of 14.
3. There is a limitation on the number of ‘Wild Cards’ a player may receive to compete in a Grand Slam Tournament.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (a) 1 and 2 only. The Grand Slam Rule Book makes minors under 14 ineligible and sets no limit on the wild cards a player may receive.

  • Statement 1: correct. Through a shared governance structure, Grand Slam Tennis is the collaboration of the four Slams, run by a board of their four chairs supported by their CEOs.
  • Statement 2: correct. The Grand Slam Rule Book opens the four tournaments to internationally ranked players on merit and without discrimination, but minors under 14 are not eligible.
  • Statement 3: incorrect. The Grand Slam Rule Book says there shall be no limitation on the number of wild cards a player may receive to compete in the Grand Slam tournaments.

The four Grand Slams are the Australian Open (hard court, Melbourne), the French Open at Roland-Garros (clay, Paris), Wimbledon (grass, London) and the US Open (hard court, New York). They follow one Grand Slam Rule Book, set by Grand Slam Tennis, their joint board. A wild card lets a tournament admit a player who does not qualify on ranking; each Slam chooses its own, and the Rule Book puts no cap on how many one player may receive.

The trap: (d) is tempting because a cap on wild cards sounds like a fair-play rule, but the Grand Slam Rule Book states plainly that there shall be no limitation on the number of wild cards a player may receive.

A note: The Rule Book's entry clause covers internationally ranked players with a ranking of 500 or better, a condition statement 2 leaves out, so some may read that statement as incomplete.

en.explanation:

The Bharat Forecast System, launched on 26 May 2025, is India's own high-resolution weather forecasting model. Its 6 km grid, against 12 km for the earlier model, sharpens short and medium range forecasts of heavy rain, cyclones and other extremes for small areas. It was built at IITM Pune, a Ministry of Earth Sciences institute, and is used by IMD for operational forecasts.

The trap: (c) is tempting because IIT Delhi does atmospheric research, but BharatFS was developed by IITM Pune, the Ministry of Earth Sciences institute behind India's weather and monsoon models.

en.text:
Which of the following statements regarding the features of blockchain technology are correct?
1. Records stored in the database may be made visible to relevant stakeholders without risk of alteration.
2. Copies of the entire database are stored on multiple computers on a network, syncing within seconds.
3. Consortium blockchain is a blend of public and private blockchains allowing selective data access.
4. Mathematical algorithms make it impossible to change or delete any data once recorded and accepted.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (c) 1, 2 and 4. A blend of public and private blockchains with selective access is a hybrid blockchain; a consortium blockchain is run jointly by a group of organisations.

  • Statement 1: correct. A blockchain is adjustably transparent: records can be shown to the stakeholders who need them, while hash-linked blocks and consensus keep them from being altered.
  • Statement 2: correct. It is a distributed ledger: each node keeps its own copy of the whole database, and the copies across the network sync within minutes or seconds as blocks are added.
  • Statement 3: incorrect. A blend of public and private chains with selective data access is a hybrid blockchain; a consortium blockchain is a permissioned network governed jointly by a group of organisations, such as banks.
  • Statement 4: correct. Each block carries a cryptographic hash of the one before it, so a change to an accepted record breaks every later link and other nodes reject it; this makes the ledger immutable.

A blockchain is a shared database spread across many computers, where new records are added only by consensus and each block is linked to the previous one by a cryptographic hash. NITI Aayog sums up its features as distributed, adjustably transparent, highly secure and immutable. By access, blockchains are public (open to all, as in Bitcoin), private (run by one organisation), consortium (run by a group of organisations) and hybrid (mixing public and private features).

The trap: (a) is tempting because a consortium chain does sit between fully public and fully private ones, but the blend of public and private chains with selective access is called a hybrid blockchain, while a consortium is defined by shared control among several organisations.

Read more: NITI Aayog, Blockchain: The India Strategy, Part I (draft discussion paper, January 2020), table 'What is blockchain?'.

en.text: An e-commerce revenue model where the seller has control over pricing but doesn’t keep products in stock and instead transfers customer orders and shipment details to a third-party supplier, who then ships the goods directly to the customer, is called:
en.explanation:
Answer: (a) Dropshipping Model. The seller sets the price and takes the order but holds no stock; the supplier ships straight to the customer.

E-commerce revenue models differ in who holds stock and who sets the price. In dropshipping the seller lists goods, sets the retail price and keeps the margin, while a third-party supplier holds stock and ships. In the affiliate model a site earns a commission for sending buyers to another seller; in the transaction fee model a platform charges a fee on each sale; in the agency model the platform sells for suppliers who set the price. India's FDI policy allows 100 percent FDI in marketplace e-commerce but not in the inventory model.

The trap: (d) is tempting because an agency platform also sells goods it does not stock, but there the supplier sets the price and the platform earns only a commission; in dropshipping the seller controls the price.

en.explanation:
Answer: (c) Access, Usage, and Quality. The RBI weights them 35, 45 and 20 percent in an index that runs from 0 to 100.

The Reserve Bank of India's Financial Inclusion Index, first released in August 2021, covers banking, investments, insurance, postal and pension services through 97 indicators, with no base year. Usage carries the most weight (45 percent), then Access (35) and Quality (20); Quality captures financial literacy, consumer protection and inequalities and deficiencies in services. A value of 0 means complete exclusion and 100 full inclusion; it was 53.9 for March 2021 and is published every July.

The trap: (d) is tempting because it begins with Access, but the RBI's other two sub-indices are Usage and Quality; affordability and transparency are not sub-indices of the FI-Index.

Read more: Reserve Bank of India (RBI), press release of 17 August 2021, Reserve Bank of India introduces the Financial Inclusion Index.

options: क्रेडिट पहुँच, बीमा गहनता, और पेंशन व्याप्ति
बैंकिंग पहुँच, GDP अंशदान, और वित्तीय साक्षरता

en.text: Which one of the following best describes the key objective of India’s ‘Open Network for Digital Commerce’ (ONDC) initiative?
options: To allow government control over all digital commerce transactions
To break the dominance of large e-commerce platforms by enabling interoperability across networks
To mandate UPI-based payments for all online transactions
en.explanation:
Answer: (c) To break the dominance of large e-commerce platforms by enabling interoperability across networks. On ONDC, a buyer on one app can buy from a seller on another.

The Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC), a not-for-profit company promoted by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), is an open set of protocols, not a platform or an app. It unbundles buyer apps, seller apps and logistics providers so that any app on the network can transact with any other, much as UPI did for payments. The aim is to democratise digital commerce, cut platform lock-in and help small sellers reach buyers online.

The trap: (b) is tempting because ONDC challenges the big platforms, but it does not replace private players: private buyer and seller apps join the network and compete on it.

Read more: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, on the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC).

en.text: Which one of the following statements about Unified Payments Interface (UPI) and Central Bank Digital Currency (Digital Rupee) is not correct?
options: UPI is a real-time payment system but Digital Rupee is akin to sovereign paper currency.

In case of UPI, settlement for end users happens instantly as the money gets immediately debited or credited but in case of Digital Rupee, there is no settlement as the wallet balance gets transferred to another wallet.
UPI transactions are recorded by banks and reflected in bank statements but in case of Digital Rupee, no data is captured in bank statements as transactions are from one wallet to another.
In both the cases (UPI and Digital Rupee), the liability lies with the users and their respective banks.
en.explanation:
Answer: (d) In both the cases (UPI and Digital Rupee), the liability lies with the users and their respective banks. The Digital Rupee, like a banknote, is a liability of the RBI.

UPI is a payment system that moves bank deposits, which are liabilities of commercial banks, between accounts in real time. The Digital Rupee (e-rupee) is India's Central Bank Digital Currency: a digital form of the rupee note, legal tender and a direct liability of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), held in wallets and paying no interest. Wallet-to-wallet payments settle at once without passing through bank accounts. The RBI began wholesale and retail pilots in November and December 2022.

The trap: (b) is tempting to pick because 'no settlement' sounds wrong for any payment, but it holds: an e-rupee transfer simply moves the token from one wallet to another and is final at once, like handing over cash.

Read more: Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Concept Note on Central Bank Digital Currency (October 2022) and Digital Rupee (e-rupee) FAQs.

hi.text: एकीकृत भुगतान इंटरफ़ेस (UPI) और केंद्रीय बैंक डिजिटल मुद्रा (डिजिटल रुपया) के बारे में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन सही नहीं है?
options: UPI एक तत्काल (real-time) भुगतान प्रणाली है, किंतु डिजिटल रुपया राष्ट्रिक (सॉवरेन) कागज़ी मुद्रा के सदृश्य है।

UPI के मामले में, धन को जैसे ही नामे डाला (debited) जाता है या जमा (credited) किया जाता है, अंतिम उपयोगकर्ताओं के लिए निपटान तत्काल हो जाता है, किंतु डिजिटल रुपया के मामले में, निपटान नहीं हो पाता है क्योंकि वॉलेट शेष का अन्य वॉलेट में अंतरण हो जाता है।

UPI लेनदेनों को बैंकों द्वारा अभिलिखित (रिकॉर्ड) किया जाता है और उन्हें बैंक विवरणों में दर्शाया जाता है, किंतु डिजिटल रुपया के मामले में, बैंक विवरणों में कोई डेटा दर्ज नहीं किया जाता है, क्योंकि लेनदेन एक वॉलेट से दूसरे वॉलेट में होते हैं।
दोनों मामलों (UPI और डिजिटल रुपया) में, उपयोगकर्ताओं और उनके संबंधित बैंकों पर देयता होती है।

en.text:
Which of the following statements about Real-World Assets (RWA) Tokenization are correct?
1. Tokenization is the process of turning real world assets into digital tokens using blockchain technology.
2. Tokenization of real world assets offers 24 × 7 access, promoting financial inclusion.
3. Tokenization of real world assets will allow the access to high growth investment opportunities for individuals in India.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (a) 1, 2 and 3. Tokenisation records a real asset on a blockchain as small, tradable tokens that can be bought at any hour by many more investors.

  • Statement 1: correct. Tokenisation represents ownership of a real-world asset, such as property, bonds, gold or art, as digital tokens on a blockchain or other distributed ledger.
  • Statement 2: correct. Tokens trade on digital platforms that need not follow market hours, giving 24x7 access, and their small sizes let people with modest savings take part.
  • Statement 3: correct. Fractional ownership cuts the ticket size, so individual investors can reach assets such as commercial real estate or private credit that were once open mainly to large investors.

Real-world asset (RWA) tokenisation turns rights over physical or financial assets into digital tokens on a blockchain. It allows fractional ownership, faster settlement, transparent records and round-the-clock trading, which can widen access and improve liquidity. Its risks include the legal status of tokens, custody, cyber security and valuation. In India, the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) consulted on a regulatory approach to RWA tokenisation in GIFT City in February 2025.

The trap: (c) is tempting if high-growth investments seem out of reach for individual investors in India, but fractional tokens cut the ticket size, so individuals can reach assets once open mainly to large investors.

Read more: International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA), Consultation Paper on Regulatory Approach towards Tokenization of Real-World Assets, February 2025.

en.text: A bond whose proceeds are used only to finance or refinance a combination of both environmental and social projects is called:
en.explanation:
Answer: (c) Sustainability Bond. Its proceeds go only to a combination of green (environmental) and social projects.

Use-of-proceeds bonds are named by what the money funds. Under the International Capital Market Association (ICMA) principles, green bonds fund only environmental projects, social bonds only social projects, and sustainability bonds a combination of both. Sustainability-linked bonds differ: the money can be used for any purpose, but the coupon depends on the issuer meeting sustainability targets. India sold its first sovereign green bonds in January 2023.

The trap: (a) is tempting because environmental projects are part of the mix, but a green bond funds only environmental projects; once social projects are funded alongside them, it is a sustainability bond.

Read more: International Capital Market Association (ICMA), Sustainability Bond Guidelines, read with the Green Bond Principles and Social Bond Principles.

en.text:
Which of the following statements about M1xchange’s role in Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) financing is/are correct?
1. M1xchange provides collateral based loans to MSMEs.
2. M1xchange facilitates discounting of invoices and Bills of Exchange for MSMEs.
3. M1xchange functions as a credit rating agency for MSMEs.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (b) 2 only. M1xchange is an RBI-licensed TReDS platform where financiers discount MSMEs' invoices and bills of exchange; it neither lends nor rates.

  • Statement 1: incorrect. M1xchange does not lend; financiers on its platform discount MSMEs' receivables from large buyers without collateral and without recourse to the MSME.
  • Statement 2: correct. Run by Mynd Solutions and licensed by the RBI, M1xchange is a Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) where banks and NBFC factors bid to discount MSMEs' invoices and bills of exchange.
  • Statement 3: incorrect. It is an electronic exchange for trade receivables, authorised under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, not a credit rating agency; rating agencies are registered with SEBI.

TReDS, set up under RBI guidelines of December 2014, is an electronic platform where MSME sellers' invoices and bills of exchange on corporate, government and PSU buyers are auctioned to banks and NBFC factors. The MSME is paid early, the financier collects from the buyer on the due date, and the deal is without recourse to the MSME. The first licensed platforms were RXIL, Invoicemart (A.TReDS) and M1xchange.

The trap: (c) is tempting because a buyer's creditworthiness drives the discount rate on TReDS, but M1xchange only runs the auction platform; it does not rate MSMEs, and rating agencies in India are registered with SEBI.

Read more: Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) guidelines of December 2014, as revised.

en.text: Which one of the following best describes the ‘Crowding Out Effect’ in the context of fiscal policy?
options: A situation where private investment increases due to increased Government spending
A situation where Government borrowing leads to higher interest rates, which reduces private investment
A situation where an increase in taxes leads to increased private sector investment
A situation where Government spending has no impact on aggregate demand
en.explanation:
Answer: (b) A situation where Government borrowing leads to higher interest rates, which reduces private investment. Government and firms compete for the same pool of savings.

When a government runs a fiscal deficit and borrows from the market, it competes with private firms for a limited pool of savings. More demand for loanable funds pushes up interest rates, which makes private projects costlier, so part of the boost from government spending is offset by lower private investment. The effect is weaker when the economy has idle resources or when the central bank keeps rates low. Public spending that draws in private investment, as on infrastructure, is called crowding in.

The trap: (a) is tempting because public spending on roads or power can attract private investment, but that is crowding in; crowding out is the opposite, private investment falling as government borrowing raises interest rates.

Read more: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy, on fiscal policy and the fiscal deficit.

hi.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा, राजकोषीय नीति के संदर्भ में ‘निजी निवेश के बहिर्गमन का प्रभाव’ (‘Crowding Out Effect’) का सर्वोत्तम वर्णन करता है?

en.text:
Which of the following statements about Rare Earth Elements (REEs) and Critical Minerals is/are correct?
1. Modern technological innovations including Artificial Intelligence, robotics and space exploration extensively utilise Rare Earth Elements (REEs).
2. China has the highest share in mining of REEs followed by India.
3. The Government of India launched the National Critical Mineral Mission (NCMM) in 2025 to establish a robust framework for self-reliance in the critical mineral sector.
4. Rare Earth Elements are a set of 13 metallic elements.
Select the answer using the code given below:
en.explanation:
Answer: (a) 1 and 3 only. China leads rare earth mining but the United States, not India, is second, and rare earths number 17, not 13.

  • Statement 1: correct. Rare earths go into strong permanent magnets, electronics and sensors used in robots, computing hardware, electric motors, defence systems and spacecraft.
  • Statement 2: incorrect. By US Geological Survey estimates, China mined about 270,000 tonnes in 2024, followed by the United States and Myanmar; India mined only about 2,900 tonnes.
  • Statement 3: correct. The Union Cabinet approved the National Critical Mineral Mission (NCMM) on 29 January 2025, with Rs 16,300 crore of government spending, for self-reliance from exploration to recycling.
  • Statement 4: incorrect. Rare earth elements are 17 metals: the 15 lanthanides plus scandium and yttrium.

Rare earth elements are 17 metals, the 15 lanthanides with scandium and yttrium, which are not truly rare but seldom occur in workable concentrations. China dominates their mining and, even more, their processing and magnet making, and its 2025 export curbs on some rare earths and magnets alarmed industries worldwide. India holds the third-largest reserves, mostly in coastal monazite sands mined by IREL (India) Limited, and launched the National Critical Mineral Mission in 2025.

The trap: (d) is tempting because India has the third-largest reserves, but it mines little: the United States, Myanmar and Australia all mine far more, and the rare earths number 17, not 13.

Read more: Ministry of Mines, PIB release of 29 January 2025 on the National Critical Mineral Mission; US Geological Survey, Mineral Commodity Summaries 2025, Rare Earths.
